verses.1:1: In the beginning the Word was, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
verses.1:2: This One was in the beginning with God.
verses.1:3: All things through Him came into being, and apart from Him came into being not even one thing. That which has come into being
verses.1:4: in Him was life, and the life was the light of men;
verses.1:5: and the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.
verses.1:6: There came a man, sent forth from God, whose name was John.
verses.1:7: This man came for witness, that he might bear witness concerning the light, that all might believe through him.
verses.1:8: He was not that light, but came that he might bear witness concerning the light.
verses.1:9: The true light, which enlightens every man, was coming into the world.
verses.1:10: He was in the world, and the world came into being through Him, yet the world did not know Him.
verses.1:11: To His own things He came, and His own people did not receive Him.
verses.1:12: Yet as many as received Him, to them He gave authority to become children of God, even to those who believe upon His name,
verses.1:13: who were begotten, not of bloods, nor of the will of flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
verses.1:14: And the Word became flesh and tabernacled among us; and we beheld His glory, glory as of an only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.
verses.1:15: (John bears witness concerning Him, and has cried out, saying, "This was He of whom I spoke, 'He who comes after me has become before me, because He was prior to me.'")
verses.1:16: For out of His fullness we all have received, even grace upon grace;
verses.1:17: because the law was given through Moses, while grace and truth came into being through Jesus Christ.
verses.1:18: No one has ever beheld God; the only-begotten God, who is in the bosom of the Father, He has made Him known.
verses.1:19: And this is the witness of John, when the Jews sent forth priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, "Who are you?"
verses.1:20: And he confessed and did not deny, yes, he confessed, "I am not the Christ."
verses.1:21: And they asked him, "What then? Are you Elijah?" And he says, "I am not." "Are you the prophet?" And he answered, "No."
verses.1:22: They said therefore to him, "Who are you, that we may give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say concerning yourself?"
verses.1:23: He said, "I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, 'Make straight the way of the Lord,' even as Isaiah the prophet said."
verses.1:24: Now those who had been sent were of the Pharisees.
verses.1:25: And they asked him and said to him, "Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?"
verses.1:26: John answered them, saying, "I baptize in water; in the midst of you stands One whom you do not know,
verses.1:27: He who comes after me, of whom I am not worthy to loose the strap of His sandal."
verses.1:28: These things came to pass in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
verses.1:29: On the next day he sees Jesus coming to him, and says, "Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
verses.1:30: This is He on whose behalf I said, 'After me comes a man who has become before me, because He was prior to me.'
verses.1:31: And I did not know Him; yet that He might be made manifest to Israel, for this cause I came baptizing in water."
verses.1:32: And John bore witness, saying, "I have beheld the Spirit descending as a dove out of heaven, and He abode upon Him.
verses.1:33: And I did not know Him; but He who sent me to baptize in water, the same said to me, 'Upon whomever you see the Spirit descending and abiding upon Him, this is He who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.'
verses.1:34: And I have seen, and have borne witness that this One is the Son of God."
verses.1:35: On the next day again John was standing, and two of his disciples;
verses.1:36: and looking upon Jesus as He walked, he says, "Behold, the Lamb of God!"
verses.1:37: And the two disciples heard him speaking, and they followed Jesus.
verses.1:38: Now Jesus, having turned and beheld them following, says to them, "What do you seek?" And they said to Him, "Rabbi (which being interpreted is called Teacher), where do You abide?"
verses.1:39: He says to them, "Come, and you shall see." They came therefore and saw where He abode, and they abode with Him that day; it was about the tenth hour.
verses.1:40: Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who heard from John and followed Him.
verses.1:41: This man finds first his own brother Simon and says to him, "We have found the Messiah" (which being interpreted is Christ).
verses.1:42: He brought him to Jesus. Looking upon him, Jesus said, "You are Simon, the son of John; you shall be called Cephas" (which is interpreted Peter).
verses.1:43: On the next day He desired to go forth into Galilee, and He finds Philip; and Jesus says to him, "Follow Me."
verses.1:44: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, of the city of Andrew and Peter.
verses.1:45: Philip finds Nathanael and says to him, "Him of whom Moses wrote in the law, and also the prophets, we have found, Jesus son of Joseph, the one from Nazareth."
verses.1:46: And Nathanael said to him, "Out of Nazareth can any good thing be?" Philip says to him, "Come and see."
verses.1:47: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to Him and says concerning him, "Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom is no deceit!"
verses.1:48: Nathanael says to Him, "From where do You know me?" Jesus answered and said to him, "Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you."
verses.1:49: Nathanael answered Him, "Rabbi, You are the Son of God; You are King of Israel!"
verses.1:50: Jesus answered and said to him, "Because I said to you that I saw you beneath the fig tree, do you believe? Greater things than these you shall see."
verses.1:51: And He says to him, "Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, you shall see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man."
verses.2:1: And on the third day a wedding took place in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.
verses.2:2: Now Jesus and His disciples were also invited to the wedding.
verses.2:3: And when the wine failed, the mother of Jesus said to Him, "They have no wine."
verses.2:4: And Jesus said to her, "What is that to Me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet arrived."
verses.2:5: His mother told the servants, "Whatever He says to you, do it."
verses.2:6: Now six stone water jars were set there according to the purification of the Jews, each holding two or three measures.
verses.2:7: Jesus said to them, "Fill the water jars with water." So they filled them to the very brim.
verses.2:8: And He said to them, "Draw some now, and bring it to the master of the banquet." And they brought it.
verses.2:9: When the master of the banquet tasted the water that had become wine, and did not know where it came from—though the servants who had drawn the water knew—the master of the banquet called the bridegroom,
verses.2:10: and said to him, "Every man sets forth the good wine first, and when they have drunk freely, then the lesser; you have reserved the good wine until now."
verses.2:11: This beginning of the signs Jesus performed in Cana of Galilee, and revealed His glory; and His disciples believed in Him.
verses.2:12: After this He went down to Capernaum—He, His mother, His brothers, and His disciples—and they did not remain there many days.
verses.2:13: And the Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
verses.2:14: And in the temple He found those who were selling oxen, sheep, and doves, and the money changers sitting there.
verses.2:15: And having made a whip of cords, He drove them all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen; and He poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned the tables.
verses.2:16: And to those who sold the doves He said, "Take these things away from here; do not make My Father's house a house of commerce."
verses.2:17: His disciples remembered that it is written, "Zeal for Your house will devour Me."
verses.2:18: Therefore the Jews answered and said to Him, "What sign do You show us, seeing that You do these things?"
verses.2:19: Jesus answered and said to them, "Tear down this temple, and in three days I will raise it up."
verses.2:20: Then the Jews said, "In forty-six years this temple was built, and will You raise it up in three days?"
verses.2:21: He, however, was speaking of the temple of His body.
verses.2:22: Therefore, when He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word which Jesus spoke.
verses.2:23: Now while He was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the feast, many believed in His name, beholding His signs which He was performing.
verses.2:24: Yet Jesus Himself did not entrust Himself to them, because He knew all men,
verses.2:25: and because He had no need that anyone should bear witness concerning man, for He Himself knew what was in man.
verses.3:1: Now there was a man from among the Pharisees, Nicodemus by name, a ruler of the Jews.
verses.3:2: This man came to Him by night and said to Him, "Rabbi, we know that You have come from God as a teacher; for no one is able to perform these signs which You do unless God is with him."
verses.3:3: Jesus answered and said to him, "Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God."
verses.3:4: Nicodemus said to Him, "How is a man able to be born when he is old? Surely he cannot enter into his mother's womb a second time and be born?"
verses.3:5: Jesus answered, "Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
verses.3:6: What is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit.
verses.3:7: Do not marvel that I told you, 'You must be born anew.'
verses.3:8: The wind blows where it wills, and you hear its sound, yet you do not know where it comes from and where it goes; thus is everyone who has been born of the Spirit."
verses.3:9: Nicodemus answered and said to Him, "How can these things come to pass?"
verses.3:10: Jesus answered and said to him, "You are the teacher of Israel, and you do not know these things?
verses.3:11: Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, what We know We speak, and what We have seen We bear witness to, yet you do not receive Our testimony.
verses.3:12: If I have spoken to you of earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I speak to you of heavenly things?
verses.3:13: And no one has ascended into heaven except He who came down from heaven, the Son of Man.
verses.3:14: And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up,
verses.3:15: that everyone who believes in Him may have eternal life.
verses.3:16: For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that everyone who believes in Him may not perish, but have eternal life.
verses.3:17: For God did not send the Son into the world that He might judge the world, but that the world might be saved through Him.
verses.3:18: He who believes in Him is not judged; yet he who does not believe has already been judged, because he has not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.
verses.3:19: And this is the judgment, that the light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light, for their works were evil.
verses.3:20: For everyone who practices wicked things hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his works be exposed.
verses.3:21: Yet he who does the truth comes to the light, that his works may be made manifest, that they have been accomplished in God."
verses.3:22: After these things Jesus and His disciples went into the land of Judea, and there He remained with them and was baptizing.
verses.3:23: Now John also was baptizing in Aenon near Salim, because abundant waters were there; and people were coming and being baptized,
verses.3:24: for John had not yet been cast into prison.
verses.3:25: Then a dispute arose on the part of John's disciples with a Jew concerning purification.
verses.3:26: And they came to John and said to him, "Rabbi, He who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you have borne witness—behold, this One is baptizing, and all are coming to Him."
verses.3:27: John answered and said, "A man cannot receive even a single thing unless it has been given to him from heaven.
verses.3:28: You yourselves bear witness for me that I said, 'I am not the Christ,' but rather, 'I have been sent before Him.'
verses.3:29: He who has the bride is the bridegroom; yet the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and listens to him, rejoices with great joy because of the bridegroom's voice. Therefore this joy of mine has been made full.
verses.3:30: He must increase, yet I must decrease."
verses.3:31: He who comes from above is over all; he who is from the earth is of the earth and speaks from the earth. He who comes from heaven is over all.
verses.3:32: What He has seen and heard, to this He bears witness, yet no one receives His testimony.
verses.3:33: He who has received His testimony has set his seal that God is true.
verses.3:34: For He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for He does not give the Spirit by measure.
verses.3:35: The Father loves the Son, and into His hand He has given all things.
verses.3:36: He who believes in the Son has eternal life; yet he who disobeys the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abides upon him.
verses.4:1: Now when the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John—
verses.4:2: although Jesus Himself was not baptizing, but rather His disciples—
verses.4:3: He departed from Judea and went away again into Galilee.
verses.4:4: And it was necessary for Him to pass through Samaria.
verses.4:5: Therefore He came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the parcel of land which Jacob gave to Joseph his son.
verses.4:6: Now the well of Jacob was there. Jesus therefore, having grown weary from the journey, was sitting thus beside the well; it was about the sixth hour.
verses.4:7: A woman from Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her, "Give Me to drink."
verses.4:8: For His disciples had departed into the city, that they might buy provisions.
verses.4:9: Therefore the Samaritan woman said to Him, "How is it that You, being a Jew, ask to drink from me, who am a Samaritan woman?" For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.
verses.4:10: Jesus answered and said to her, "If you had known the gift of God, and who He is who says to you, 'Give Me to drink,' you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water."
verses.4:11: The woman said to Him, "Sir, You have no vessel to draw with, and the well is deep; where then do You obtain this living water?
verses.4:12: Are You greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well, and drank from it himself, as well as his sons and his livestock?"
verses.4:13: Jesus answered and said to her, "Everyone who drinks of this water shall thirst again;
verses.4:14: but whoever drinks of the water which I shall give him shall never thirst; rather, the water which I shall give him shall become within him a fountain of water welling up into eternal life."
verses.4:15: The woman said to Him, "Sir, give me this water, that I may neither thirst nor come all the way here to draw."
verses.4:16: He said to her, "Go, summon your husband, and come here."
verses.4:17: The woman answered and said to Him, "I have no husband." Jesus said to her, "You have spoken rightly in saying, 'I have no husband';
verses.4:18: for you have had five husbands, and the one whom you now have is not your husband; this you have spoken truthfully."
verses.4:19: The woman said to Him, "Sir, I discern that You are a prophet.
verses.4:20: Our fathers worshiped upon this mountain, and you say that in Jerusalem is the place where one must worship."
verses.4:21: Jesus said to her, "Believe Me, woman, an hour is coming when neither upon this mountain nor in Jerusalem shall you worship the Father.
verses.4:22: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because salvation is from the Jews.
verses.4:23: Yet an hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth; for indeed the Father seeks such as these to worship Him.
verses.4:24: God is Spirit, and it is necessary for those who worship Him to worship in spirit and truth."
verses.4:25: The woman said to Him, "I know that Messiah is coming—He who is called Christ; when that One comes, He will declare all things to us."
verses.4:26: Jesus said to her, "I am He, the One who speaks to you."
verses.4:27: And upon this His disciples arrived, and they were marveling that He was speaking with a woman; yet no one said, "What do You seek?" or "Why are You speaking with her?"
verses.4:28: Therefore the woman left her water jar and went away into the city, and said to the people,
verses.4:29: "Come, see a man who told me all the things that I did! Could this possibly be the Christ?"
verses.4:30: They went out from the city and were coming toward Him.
verses.4:31: Meanwhile the disciples were urging Him, saying, "Rabbi, eat."
verses.4:32: But He said to them, "I have food to eat which you do not know."
verses.4:33: Therefore the disciples were saying to one another, "Could anyone have brought Him something to eat?"
verses.4:34: Jesus said to them, "My food is that I should do the will of Him who sent Me, and accomplish His work.
verses.4:35: Do you not say, 'There are still four months, and the harvest comes'? Behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes and look upon the fields, for they are white for harvest. Already
verses.4:36: the reaper receives wages and gathers fruit for eternal life, that both the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.
verses.4:37: For in this the saying is true: 'One is the sower, and another is the reaper.'
verses.4:38: I sent you to reap that for which you have not toiled; others have toiled, and you have entered into their labor."
verses.4:39: Now many of the Samaritans from that city believed in Him on account of the word of the woman who testified, "He told me all things that I did."
verses.4:40: Therefore, when the Samaritans came to Him, they implored Him to remain with them; and He remained there two days.
verses.4:41: And far more believed on account of His word,
verses.4:42: and they were saying to the woman, "We no longer believe because of your report; for we ourselves have heard, and we know that this One is truly the Savior of the world."
verses.4:43: Now after the two days He went forth from there into Galilee.
verses.4:44: For Jesus Himself bore witness that a prophet has no honor in his own homeland.
verses.4:45: Therefore, when He arrived in Galilee, the Galileans welcomed Him, having beheld all the things which He had done in Jerusalem during the feast; for they themselves had also gone to the feast.
verses.4:46: Therefore He came again into Cana of Galilee, where He had made the water wine. And there was a certain royal official whose son was ill in Capernaum.
verses.4:47: This man, having heard that Jesus had come from Judea into Galilee, went away to Him and pleaded that He would come down and heal his son; for he was about to die.
verses.4:48: Jesus therefore said to him, "Unless you behold signs and wonders, you shall by no means believe."
verses.4:49: The royal official said to Him, "Sir, come down before my little child dies!"
verses.4:50: Jesus said to him, "Go; your son lives." The man believed the word which Jesus spoke to him, and went on his way.
verses.4:51: And while he was already going down, his servants met him, saying that his boy lives.
verses.4:52: Therefore he inquired of them the hour at which he began to mend. So they said to him, "Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him."
verses.4:53: The father therefore knew that it was at that very hour in which Jesus had said to him, "Your son lives"; and he himself believed, and his entire household.
verses.4:54: Now this again was the second sign that Jesus performed, having come from Judea into Galilee.
verses.5:1: After these things there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
verses.5:2: Now there is in Jerusalem, beside the Sheep Gate, a pool called in Hebrew Bethzatha, which has five porticoes.
verses.5:3: In these lay a multitude of the sick—blind, lame, and withered.
verses.5:5: Now a certain man was there who had been in his infirmity for thirty-eight years.
verses.5:6: When Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he had already been so for a long time, He said to him, "Do you wish to be made whole?"
verses.5:7: The infirm man answered Him, "Sir, I have no man to put me into the pool whenever the water is troubled; but while I am coming, another goes down before me."
verses.5:8: Jesus said to him, "Arise, take up your mat, and walk."
verses.5:9: And immediately the man was made whole, and took up his mat and walked. Now that day was the Sabbath.
verses.5:10: Therefore the Jews said to him who had been healed, "It is the Sabbath, and it is not lawful for you to carry the mat."
verses.5:11: But he answered them, "He who made me whole—He said to me, 'Take up your mat and walk.'"
verses.5:12: They asked him, "Who is the man who said to you, 'Take up and walk'?"
verses.5:13: Now the man who had been healed did not know who He was, for Jesus had slipped away, since a multitude was in that place.
verses.5:14: After these things Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, "Behold, you have been made whole. Sin no more, lest something worse befall you."
verses.5:15: The man departed and reported to the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him whole.
verses.5:16: And for this cause the Jews were persecuting Jesus, because He was doing these things on the Sabbath.
verses.5:17: But He answered them, "My Father is working until now, and I also am working."
verses.5:18: For this reason, therefore, the Jews sought all the more to kill Him, because He was not only breaking the Sabbath, but also calling God His own Father, making Himself equal with God.
verses.5:19: Therefore Jesus answered and said to them, "Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, the Son cannot do anything of Himself, except what He sees the Father doing; for whatever He does, these things the Son also does in like manner.
verses.5:20: For the Father loves the Son and shows Him all that He Himself is doing; and greater works than these He will show Him, so that you may marvel.
verses.5:21: For just as the Father raises the dead and gives life, so also the Son gives life to whom He wills.
verses.5:22: For not even the Father judges anyone, but He has given all judgment to the Son,
verses.5:23: so that all may honor the Son, even as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.
verses.5:24: Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, he who hears My word and believes Him who sent Me has eternal life, and does not come into judgment, but has crossed over out of death into life.
verses.5:25: Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, an hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear shall live.
verses.5:26: For just as the Father has life in Himself, so He also gave to the Son to have life in Himself;
verses.5:27: and He gave Him authority to execute judgment, because He is the Son of Man.
verses.5:28: Do not marvel at this, for an hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs shall hear His voice
verses.5:29: and shall come forth—those who have done good to a resurrection of life, and those who have practiced evil to a resurrection of judgment.
verses.5:30: I am able to do nothing on My own; just as I hear, I judge, and My judgment is righteous, because I do not seek My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me.
verses.5:31: If I bear witness concerning Myself, My testimony is not true.
verses.5:32: There is Another who bears witness concerning Me, and I know that the testimony He bears concerning Me is true.
verses.5:33: You yourselves have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
verses.5:34: Yet I do not accept testimony from man, but I speak these things so that you may be saved.
verses.5:35: He was the lamp that was burning and shining, and you were willing to rejoice for an hour in his light.
verses.5:36: But the testimony I have is greater than that of John; for the works that the Father has given Me to accomplish—these very works that I am doing—bear witness concerning Me, that the Father has sent Me.
verses.5:37: And the Father who sent Me, He Himself has borne witness concerning Me. Neither have you heard His voice at any time, nor have you seen His form,
verses.5:38: and you do not have His word abiding in you, because you do not believe the One whom He sent.
verses.5:39: You search the Scriptures, because you suppose that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that bear witness concerning Me;
verses.5:40: and yet you are unwilling to come to Me, so that you may have life.
verses.5:41: I do not receive glory from men,
verses.5:42: but I know you, that you do not have the love of God within yourselves.
verses.5:43: I have come in the name of My Father, and you do not receive Me; if another should come in his own name, that one you will receive.
verses.5:44: How are you able to believe, when you receive glory from one another, and do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?
verses.5:45: Do not suppose that I shall accuse you before the Father; the one who accuses you is Moses, in whom you have set your hope.
verses.5:46: For if you believed Moses, you would believe Me, for he wrote concerning Me.
verses.5:47: Yet if you do not believe his writings, how shall you believe My words?"
verses.6:1: After these things Jesus departed across the Sea of Galilee, that is, the Sea of Tiberias.
verses.6:2: And a great multitude was following Him, because they beheld the signs which He was performing on those who were sick.
verses.6:3: Now Jesus ascended the mountain, and there He sat with His disciples.
verses.6:4: And the Passover, the feast of the Jews, was near.
verses.6:5: Therefore, lifting up His eyes and beholding that a great multitude was coming to Him, Jesus said to Philip, "Where shall we buy bread, so that these people may eat?"
verses.6:6: Now He was saying this to test him, for He Himself knew what He was about to do.
verses.6:7: Philip answered Him, "Bread worth two hundred denarii does not suffice for them, that each one may receive a little."
verses.6:8: One of His disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, said to Him,
verses.6:9: "There is a young boy here who has five barley loaves and two small fish; yet what are these among so many?"
verses.6:10: Jesus said, "Have the people recline." Now there was abundant grass in the place. Therefore the men reclined, about five thousand in number.
verses.6:11: Then Jesus took the loaves, and having given thanks, He distributed them to those who were reclining; and likewise of the small fish, as much as they desired.
verses.6:12: And when they were filled, He said to His disciples, "Gather the leftover fragments, lest anything be lost."
verses.6:13: So they gathered them and filled twelve baskets with fragments from the five barley loaves, which remained over from those who had eaten.
verses.6:14: Therefore, when the people saw the sign which He had performed, they were saying, "This is truly the Prophet who is coming into the world."
verses.6:15: Knowing, therefore, that they were about to come and seize Him in order to make Him king, Jesus withdrew again to the mountain by Himself alone.
verses.6:16: And when evening fell, His disciples went down to the sea,
verses.6:17: and embarking in a boat, they were crossing over the sea toward Capernaum. Now darkness had already fallen, and Jesus had not yet come to them,
verses.6:18: and the sea was being stirred up as a great wind was blowing.
verses.6:19: When they had rowed, therefore, about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they beheld Jesus walking upon the sea and drawing near to the boat; and they became afraid.
verses.6:20: And He said to them, "It is I; do not fear."
verses.6:21: Therefore they were willing to receive Him into the boat, and at once the boat was at the land toward which they were going.
verses.6:22: On the next day, the multitude that stood on the far side of the sea saw that no other small boat had been there except one, and that Jesus had not embarked in the boat with His disciples, but His disciples had departed alone.
verses.6:23: Other small boats came from Tiberias near the place where they had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
verses.6:24: When the multitude therefore saw that Jesus was not there, nor His disciples, they themselves embarked in the small boats and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.
verses.6:25: And having found Him across the sea, they said to Him, "Rabbi, when did You arrive here?"
verses.6:26: Jesus answered them and said, "Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, you seek Me not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were satisfied.
verses.6:27: Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that abides to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you; for upon Him God the Father has set His seal."
verses.6:28: Therefore they said to Him, "What are we to do, that we may work the works of God?"
verses.6:29: Jesus answered and said to them, "This is the work of God: that you believe in the One whom He sent."
verses.6:30: Therefore they said to Him, "What sign, then, do You perform, so that we may see and believe You? What work do You do?
verses.6:31: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, just as it is written, 'Bread from heaven He gave them to eat.'"
verses.6:32: Jesus therefore said to them, "Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, it is not Moses who has given you the bread from heaven, but My Father gives you the true bread from heaven;
verses.6:33: for the bread of God is He who descends from heaven and gives life to the world."
verses.6:34: Therefore they said to Him, "Lord, give us this bread at all times."
verses.6:35: Jesus said to them, "I am the bread of life; whoever comes to Me shall by no means hunger, and whoever believes in Me shall never thirst.
verses.6:36: Yet I told you that you have indeed seen Me, and still you do not believe."
verses.6:37: "All that the Father gives to Me shall come to Me, and whoever comes to Me I shall by no means cast out,
verses.6:38: for I have descended from heaven, not to do My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me.
verses.6:39: Now this is the will of Him who sent Me, that of all that He has given to Me I should lose none, but should raise it up on the last day.
verses.6:40: For this is the will of My Father: that everyone who beholds the Son and believes in Him should have eternal life, and I Myself shall raise him up on the last day."
verses.6:41: Therefore the Jews were murmuring about Him because He said, "I am the bread that descended from heaven,"
verses.6:42: and they were saying, "Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How does He now say, 'I have descended from heaven'?"
verses.6:43: Jesus answered and said to them, "Do not murmur with one another.
verses.6:44: No one is able to come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him; and I shall raise him up on the last day.
verses.6:45: It is written in the Prophets, 'And all of them shall be taught by God.' Everyone who has heard from the Father and learned comes to Me.
verses.6:46: Not that anyone has seen the Father, except the One who is from God; this One has seen the Father.
verses.6:47: Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, the one who believes has eternal life.
verses.6:48: I am the bread of life.
verses.6:49: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and died.
verses.6:50: This is the bread that descends from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die.
verses.6:51: I am the living bread that descended from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he shall live forever; and the bread that I will give is My flesh, for the life of the world."
verses.6:52: Therefore the Jews were contending with one another, saying, "How can this man give us His flesh to eat?"
verses.6:53: Jesus therefore said to them, "Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you do not have life in yourselves.
verses.6:54: The one who eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I Myself shall raise him up on the last day.
verses.6:55: For My flesh is true food, and My blood is true drink.
verses.6:56: The one who eats My flesh and drinks My blood abides in Me, and I in him.
verses.6:57: Just as the living Father sent Me, and I live because of the Father, so also the one who eats Me shall live because of Me.
verses.6:58: This is the bread that descended from heaven, not as the fathers ate and died; the one who eats this bread shall live forever."
verses.6:59: These things He spoke in a synagogue while teaching in Capernaum.
verses.6:60: Many of His disciples, therefore, upon hearing this, said, "This saying is hard; who is able to listen to it?"
verses.6:61: Now Jesus, knowing within Himself that His disciples were murmuring about this, said to them, "Does this cause you to stumble?
verses.6:62: What, then, if you should behold the Son of Man ascending to where He was before?
verses.6:63: The Spirit is the One who gives life; the flesh avails nothing. The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and are life.
verses.6:64: Yet there are some among you who do not believe." For Jesus knew from the beginning which ones did not believe, and who it was that would betray Him.
verses.6:65: And He was saying, "For this reason I have told you that no one is able to come to Me unless it has been granted to him from the Father."
verses.6:66: From that time many of His disciples turned back and no longer walked with Him.
verses.6:67: Jesus therefore said to the Twelve, "Do you also wish to depart?"
verses.6:68: Simon Peter answered Him, "Lord, to whom shall we go? You have words of eternal life,
verses.6:69: and we ourselves have believed and come to know that You are the Holy One of God."
verses.6:70: Jesus answered them, "Did I Myself not choose you, the Twelve? Yet one among you is a devil."
verses.6:71: Now He was speaking of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot; for he was about to betray Him, one of the Twelve.
verses.7:1: And after these things Jesus went about in Galilee; for He did not wish to walk in Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill Him.
verses.7:2: Now the feast of the Jews, the Feast of Tabernacles, was at hand.
verses.7:3: Therefore His brothers said to Him, "Depart from this place and go into Judea, so that Your disciples also may behold Your works which You are doing;
verses.7:4: for no one does anything in secret and yet himself seeks to be in the open. If You are doing these things, manifest Yourself to the world."
verses.7:5: For not even His brothers were believing in Him.
verses.7:6: Jesus therefore said to them, "My time is not yet here, but your time is always ready.
verses.7:7: The world cannot hate you, yet it hates Me, because I bear witness concerning it that its works are evil.
verses.7:8: You go up to the feast; I am not yet going up to this feast, because My time has not yet been fulfilled."
verses.7:9: And having said these things to them, He remained in Galilee.
verses.7:10: But when His brothers had gone up to the feast, then He Himself also went up, not openly, but as it were in secret.
verses.7:11: Therefore the Jews were seeking Him at the feast and saying, "Where is He?"
verses.7:12: And there was much murmuring concerning Him among the multitudes: some were saying, "He is good," while others were saying, "No, rather He leads the multitude astray."
verses.7:13: Yet no one spoke openly concerning Him for fear of the Jews.
verses.7:14: Now when the feast was already half over, Jesus went up into the temple and was teaching.
verses.7:15: Therefore the Jews marveled, saying, "How does this Man know letters, not having studied?"
verses.7:16: Jesus therefore answered them and said, "My teaching is not My own, but His who sent Me.
verses.7:17: If anyone is willing to do His will, he shall know concerning the teaching, whether it is of God or whether I speak from Myself.
verses.7:18: The one who speaks on his own seeks his own glory; but He who seeks the glory of the One who sent Him, this One is true, and there is no unrighteousness in Him.
verses.7:19: Has not Moses given you the law? Yet none of you keeps the law. Why do you seek to kill Me?"
verses.7:20: The multitude answered, "You have a demon. Who is seeking to kill You?"
verses.7:21: Jesus answered and said to them, "One work I did, and you all marvel.
verses.7:22: Because of this Moses has given you circumcision—not that it is from Moses, but from the fathers—and on the Sabbath you circumcise a man.
verses.7:23: If a man receives circumcision on the Sabbath lest the law of Moses be broken, are you angry with Me because I made a whole man well on the Sabbath?
verses.7:24: Do not judge by appearance, but judge righteous judgment."
verses.7:25: Therefore some of the people of Jerusalem were saying, "Is this not He whom they are seeking to kill?
verses.7:26: And behold, He speaks openly, and they say nothing to Him! Can it be that the rulers have truly come to know that this is the Christ?
verses.7:27: Yet as for this Man, we know where He is from; but when the Christ comes, no one knows where He is from."
verses.7:28: Therefore Jesus cried out as He was teaching in the temple, saying, "Indeed you know Me, and you know where I am from; yet I have not come from Myself, but the One who sent Me is true, whom you do not know.
verses.7:29: I know Him, because I am from Him, and He sent Me."
verses.7:30: Therefore they sought to seize Him, and no one laid his hand on Him, because His hour had not yet arrived.
verses.7:31: Yet many from the multitude believed in Him, and were saying, "When the Christ comes, will He perform more signs than those which this Man has done?"
verses.7:32: The Pharisees heard the multitude murmuring these things concerning Him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to seize Him.
verses.7:33: Therefore Jesus said, "For a little while longer I am with you, and then I am going to Him who sent Me.
verses.7:34: You will seek Me and shall not find Me; and where I am, you cannot come."
verses.7:35: Therefore the Jews said among themselves, "Where does this Man intend to go that we will not find Him? Is He about to go to the Dispersion among the Greeks and teach the Greeks?
verses.7:36: What is this saying which He spoke, 'You will seek Me and shall not find Me; and where I am, you cannot come'?"
verses.7:37: Now on the last day, the great day of the feast, Jesus was standing, and He cried out, saying, "If anyone thirsts, let him come to Me and drink.
verses.7:38: The one who believes in Me, just as the Scripture has said, out of his innermost being shall flow rivers of living water."
verses.7:39: Now this He spoke concerning the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were about to receive; for the Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
verses.7:40: Therefore some from the multitude, when they heard these words, were saying, "This is truly the Prophet."
verses.7:41: Others were saying, "This is the Christ." Yet some were saying, "Surely the Christ does not come from Galilee?
verses.7:42: Did not the Scripture say that the Christ comes from the seed of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?"
verses.7:43: Therefore a division arose among the multitude on account of Him.
verses.7:44: And some of them desired to seize Him, yet no one laid hands upon Him.
verses.7:45: The officers therefore came to the chief priests and Pharisees, and they said to them, "Why did you not bring Him?"
verses.7:46: The officers answered, "Never has a man spoken like this!"
verses.7:47: Therefore the Pharisees answered them, "Have you also been led astray?
verses.7:48: Has anyone among the rulers believed in Him, or among the Pharisees?
verses.7:49: Yet this multitude, which does not know the law, is accursed."
verses.7:50: Nicodemus—the one who had come to Him previously, being one of them—said to them,
verses.7:51: "Does our law judge a man unless it first hears from him and learns what he is doing?"
verses.7:52: They answered and said to him, "Are you also from Galilee? Search and see that no prophet arises out of Galilee."
verses.7:53: ⟦And each man departed to his own house;⟧
verses.8:1: ⟦but Jesus departed to the Mount of Olives.⟧
verses.8:2: ⟦And at dawn He came again into the temple, and all the people were coming; and having sat down, He was teaching them.⟧
verses.8:3: ⟦Now the scribes and the Pharisees bring to Him a woman caught in adultery; and having set her in the midst,⟧
verses.8:4: ⟦they say to Him, testing Him, "Teacher, this woman was caught in the very act, committing adultery.⟧
verses.8:5: ⟦Now in the law Moses commanded us that such women should be stoned; what therefore do You say?"⟧
verses.8:6: ⟦And this they were saying to test Him, that they might have cause to accuse Him. But Jesus, stooping down, wrote with His finger upon the ground, taking no heed.⟧
verses.8:7: ⟦Yet as they continued asking Him, He lifted Himself up and said to them, "Let him who is without sin among you cast the stone at her first."⟧
verses.8:8: ⟦And stooping down again, He wrote upon the ground.⟧
verses.8:9: ⟦And they, having heard, and being convicted by their conscience, went out one by one, beginning from the elders; and Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the midst.⟧
verses.8:10: ⟦And Jesus, lifting Himself up and beholding no one save the woman, said to her, "Where are those accusers of yours? Has no one condemned you?"⟧
verses.8:11: ⟦And she said, "No one, Lord." And Jesus said, "Neither do I judge you; go, and sin no more."⟧
verses.8:12: Therefore Jesus spoke to them again, saying, "I am the light of the world. The one who follows Me shall by no means walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life."
verses.8:13: Therefore the Pharisees said to Him, "You bear witness concerning Yourself; Your testimony is not true."
verses.8:14: Jesus answered and said to them, "Even if I bear witness concerning Myself, My testimony is true, for I know where I came from and where I am going; yet you do not know where I come from or where I am going.
verses.8:15: You pass judgment according to the flesh; I do not judge anyone.
verses.8:16: Yet even if I do judge, My judgment is true, because I am not alone, but it is I and the Father who sent Me.
verses.8:17: Moreover, in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two men is true.
verses.8:18: I am the One who bears witness concerning Myself, and the Father who sent Me bears witness concerning Me."
verses.8:19: Therefore they said to Him, "Where is Your Father?" Jesus answered, "You know neither Me nor My Father; if you knew Me, you would know My Father as well."
verses.8:20: He spoke these words in the treasury as He taught in the temple; yet no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet come.
verses.8:21: Therefore He said to them again, "I am going away, and you shall seek Me, and in your sin you shall die. Where I am going, you cannot come."
verses.8:22: Therefore the Jews said, "Will He kill Himself, since He says, 'Where I am going, you cannot come'?"
verses.8:23: And He said to them, "You are from beneath, and I am from above; you are from this world, and I am not from this world.
verses.8:24: Therefore I told you that you shall die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am, you shall die in your sins."
verses.8:25: Therefore they said to Him, "Who are You?" Jesus said to them, "Why do I even speak to you at all?
verses.8:26: I have many things to speak and to judge concerning you; yet He who sent Me is true, and the things that I heard from Him, these I speak to the world."
verses.8:27: They did not realize that He was speaking to them concerning the Father.
verses.8:28: Therefore Jesus said to them, "When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you shall know that I am, and that I do nothing of Myself, but just as the Father taught Me, these things I speak.
verses.8:29: And He who sent Me is with Me; He has not left Me alone, because I always do the things that are pleasing to Him."
verses.8:30: While He was speaking these things, many believed in Him.
verses.8:31: Therefore Jesus said to those Jews who had believed Him, "If you abide in My word, truly you are My disciples,
verses.8:32: and you shall know the truth, and the truth shall set you free."
verses.8:33: They answered Him, "We are the seed of Abraham, and have never at any time been in bondage to anyone. How do You say, 'You shall become free'?"
verses.8:34: Jesus answered them, "Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.
verses.8:35: Now the slave does not abide in the house forever; the son abides forever.
verses.8:36: Therefore if the Son sets you free, you shall be truly free.
verses.8:37: I know that you are the seed of Abraham; yet you seek to kill Me, because My word finds no place in you.
verses.8:38: I speak the things that I have seen with the Father; and you therefore do the things that you heard from the father."
verses.8:39: They answered and said to Him, "Our father is Abraham." Jesus said to them, "If you were children of Abraham, you would be doing the works of Abraham;
verses.8:40: but now you seek to kill Me, a man who has spoken to you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.
verses.8:41: You do the works of your father." They said to Him, "We were not born of fornication; we have one Father—God."
verses.8:42: Jesus said to them, "If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I came forth from God and am here; for neither have I come of Myself, but He sent Me.
verses.8:43: Why do you not understand My speech? Because you are unable to hear My word.
verses.8:44: You are of your father the devil, and you wish to carry out the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning, and has not stood in the truth, because there is no truth in him. Whenever he speaks falsehood, he speaks out of what is his own, for he is a liar and the father of it.
verses.8:45: Yet because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me.
verses.8:46: Which one of you convicts Me concerning sin? If I speak truth, why do you not believe Me?
verses.8:47: The one who is of God hears the words of God; for this reason you do not hear, because you are not of God."
verses.8:48: The Jews answered and said to Him, "Do we not rightly declare that You are a Samaritan and have a demon?"
verses.8:49: Jesus answered, "I do not have a demon; rather, I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me.
verses.8:50: Yet I do not seek My glory; there is One who seeks and judges.
verses.8:51: Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, if anyone keeps My word, he shall never behold death."
verses.8:52: The Jews said to Him, "Now we know that You have a demon! Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet You say, 'If anyone keeps My word, he shall never taste death.'
verses.8:53: Surely You are not greater than our father Abraham, who died? And the prophets died. Who do You make Yourself out to be?"
verses.8:54: Jesus answered, "If I glorify Myself, My glory is nothing. It is My Father who glorifies Me, of whom you say, 'He is our God,'
verses.8:55: yet you have not known Him. But I know Him; and even if I should say that I do not know Him, I shall be a liar like you. Rather, I do know Him, and I keep His word.
verses.8:56: Your father Abraham rejoiced greatly that he would see My day, and he saw it and was glad."
verses.8:57: Therefore the Jews said to Him, "You are not yet fifty years old, and You have seen Abraham?"
verses.8:58: Jesus said to them, "Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, before Abraham came into being, I am."
verses.8:59: Therefore they took up stones to cast at Him; but Jesus hid Himself and went out from the temple.
verses.9:1: And as He passed along, He saw a man blind from his birth.
verses.9:2: And His disciples questioned Him, saying, "Rabbi, who sinned—this man or his parents—that he should be born blind?"
verses.9:3: Jesus replied, "Neither this man sinned nor his parents, but that the works of God might be made manifest in him.
verses.9:4: We must perform the works of Him who sent Me while it is day; night is coming when no one is able to work.
verses.9:5: So long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world."
verses.9:6: Having spoken these things, He spat on the ground and made clay out of the saliva, and He anointed his eyes with the clay,
verses.9:7: and said to him, "Go and wash in the pool of Siloam" (which is interpreted, "Sent"). Therefore he went away and washed, and returned seeing.
verses.9:8: Therefore the neighbors and those who previously had seen him, that he was a beggar, were saying, "Is this not the one who used to sit and beg?"
verses.9:9: Some were saying, "This is the man." Others were saying, "No, rather he resembles him." He himself kept saying, "I am he."
verses.9:10: So they were saying to him, "How were your eyes opened?"
verses.9:11: He answered, "The man who is called Jesus made clay and anointed my eyes, and said to me, 'Go to Siloam and wash.' Therefore I departed and washed, and I received my sight."
verses.9:12: And they said to him, "Where is He?" He answered, "I do not know."
verses.9:13: They brought the man who had once been blind to the Pharisees.
verses.9:14: Now it was a Sabbath on the day that Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes.
verses.9:15: So the Pharisees also questioned him again how he had received his sight. And he said to them, "He laid clay upon my eyes, and I washed, and I see."
verses.9:16: Therefore some of the Pharisees were saying, "This man is not from God, because He does not observe the Sabbath." Others were saying, "How can a sinful man perform such signs?" And there was a division among them.
verses.9:17: So they spoke to the blind man again: "What do you yourself say concerning Him, since He opened your eyes?" And he answered, "He is a prophet."
verses.9:18: Therefore the Jews did not believe concerning him that he had been blind and had gained his sight, until they summoned the parents of the man who had received his sight,
verses.9:19: and questioned them, saying, "Is this your son, of whom you say that he was born blind? How then does he see now?"
verses.9:20: So his parents answered and said, "We know that this man is our son and that he was born blind;
verses.9:21: but how he now sees we do not know, nor do we ourselves know who opened his eyes. Question him; he is of age; he himself shall speak for himself."
verses.9:22: His parents spoke these things because they feared the Jews, for the Jews had already agreed among themselves that if anyone confessed Him to be the Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.
verses.9:23: For this reason his parents said, "He is of age; question him."
verses.9:24: So they summoned a second time the man who had been blind and said to him, "Give glory to God! We ourselves know that this man is a sinner."
verses.9:25: Therefore he replied, "Whether He is a sinner I do not know; this one thing I know, that though I was blind, I now see."
verses.9:26: Therefore they said to him, "What did He do to you? How did He open your eyes?"
verses.9:27: He replied to them, "I have told you already, and you did not listen. Why do you desire to hear it again? Do you yourselves also wish to become His disciples?"
verses.9:28: And they reviled him and said, "You yourself are His disciple, but we are disciples of Moses.
verses.9:29: We know that God has spoken to Moses; yet as for this man, we do not know where He is from."
verses.9:30: The man answered and said to them, "Why, in this lies the marvel, that you yourselves do not know where He is from, and yet He opened my eyes.
verses.9:31: We know that God does not listen to sinners; rather, if anyone is a worshiper of God and carries out His will, He listens to him.
verses.9:32: Never since the world began has it been heard that anyone opened the eyes of one born blind.
verses.9:33: If this man were not from God, He would be able to do nothing."
verses.9:34: They replied and said to him, "You were born wholly in sins, and are you teaching us?" And they cast him out.
verses.9:35: Jesus heard that they had cast him out, and when He found him, He said, "Do you yourself believe in the Son of Man?"
verses.9:36: He answered and said, "And who is He, Lord, so that I may believe in Him?"
verses.9:37: Jesus said to him, "You have both seen Him, and the One who speaks with you is He."
verses.9:38: And he said, "I believe, Lord!" And he worshiped Him.
verses.9:39: And Jesus said, "For judgment I came into this world, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind."
verses.9:40: Some of the Pharisees who were with Him heard these things, and they said to Him, "Surely we are not blind also?"
verses.9:41: Jesus said to them, "If you were blind, you would not have sin; yet now you say, 'We see.' Your sin abides."
verses.10:1: "Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, he who does not enter through the door into the fold of the sheep, but climbs over from another place, that man is a thief and a robber.
verses.10:2: Yet he who enters through the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
verses.10:3: For him the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep listen to his voice; and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them forth.
verses.10:4: When he has brought forth all his own, he walks before them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.
verses.10:5: A stranger, however, they will by no means follow, but will flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers."
verses.10:6: Jesus spoke this figure of speech to them, yet they did not understand what things He was speaking to them.
verses.10:7: Therefore Jesus spoke to them again: "Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, I am the door of the sheep.
verses.10:8: All, as many as came before Me, are thieves and robbers; yet the sheep did not listen to them.
verses.10:9: I am the door; if anyone enters through Me, he shall be saved, and shall go in and go out and shall find pasture.
verses.10:10: The thief does not come except that he may steal and slay and destroy; I came that they may have life, and may have it in abundance.
verses.10:11: I am the good Shepherd; the good Shepherd lays down His life on behalf of the sheep.
verses.10:12: The hireling, who is not a shepherd and to whom the sheep do not belong, beholds the wolf coming and abandons the sheep and flees—and the wolf snatches them and scatters them—
verses.10:13: because he is a hireling and has no concern for the sheep.
verses.10:14: I am the good Shepherd, and I know My own, and My own know Me,
verses.10:15: even as the Father knows Me and I know the Father; and I lay down My life on behalf of the sheep.
verses.10:16: And I have other sheep that are not of this fold; those also I must bring, and they shall hear My voice, and they shall become one flock, one Shepherd.
verses.10:17: For this cause the Father loves Me, because I lay down My life that I may take it again.
verses.10:18: No one has taken it from Me; rather, I lay it down of Myself. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it again. This commandment I received from My Father."
verses.10:19: A division arose once more among the Jews on account of these words.
verses.10:20: And many among them were saying, "He has a demon and is mad. Why are you listening to Him?"
verses.10:21: Others were saying, "These words are not those of one possessed by a demon. Can a demon possibly open the eyes of the blind?"
verses.10:22: Then the Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem; it was winter,
verses.10:23: and Jesus was walking in the temple, in the portico of Solomon.
verses.10:24: Therefore the Jews encircled Him and were saying to Him, "How long do You keep our souls in suspense? If You are the Christ, tell us plainly."
verses.10:25: Jesus answered them, "I told you, and yet you do not believe. The works that I do in the name of My Father, these testify concerning Me.
verses.10:26: Yet you do not believe, because you are not of My sheep.
verses.10:27: My sheep listen to My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me;
verses.10:28: and I give eternal life to them, and they shall by no means ever perish, and no one shall snatch them from My hand.
verses.10:29: That which My Father has given Me is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch them from the Father's hand.
verses.10:30: The Father and I are one."
verses.10:31: Again the Jews took up stones in order to stone Him.
verses.10:32: Jesus answered them, "I have shown you many good works from the Father; for which work among them are you stoning Me?"
verses.10:33: The Jews answered Him, "For a good work we are not stoning You, but for blasphemy, and because You, being a man, make Yourself God."
verses.10:34: Jesus answered them, "Does it not stand written in your law, 'I said, You are gods'?
verses.10:35: If He called those gods to whom the word of God came—and the Scripture cannot be broken—
verses.10:36: concerning Him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, do you say, 'You blaspheme,' because I said, 'I am the Son of God'?
verses.10:37: If I am not doing the works of My Father, do not believe Me;
verses.10:38: but if I am doing them, even if you do not believe Me, believe the works, so that you may know and continue to know that the Father is in Me, and I in the Father."
verses.10:39: Therefore they tried once again to seize Him, yet He escaped from their hand.
verses.10:40: And He departed once more beyond the Jordan to the place where John was first baptizing, and He remained there.
verses.10:41: And many came to Him and were saying, "John indeed performed no sign, yet all that John spoke concerning this Man was true."
verses.10:42: And there many believed in Him.
verses.11:1: Now there was a certain man who was sick, Lazarus of Bethany, from the village of Mary and Martha her sister.
verses.11:2: Now it was Mary who anointed the Lord with fragrant ointment and wiped His feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus lay sick.
verses.11:3: So the sisters sent word to Him, saying, "Lord, behold, the one You love is sick."
verses.11:4: And when Jesus heard it, He said, "This sickness is not to end in death, but is for the sake of the glory of God, that through it the Son of God may be glorified."
verses.11:5: And Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.
verses.11:6: Therefore, when He heard that he was sick, He then remained two days in the place where He was.
verses.11:7: Then after this, He said to the disciples, "Let us go again into Judea."
verses.11:8: The disciples said to Him, "Rabbi, only just now the Jews were seeking to stone You, and are You going there again?"
verses.11:9: Jesus replied, "Are there not twelve hours of the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, for he sees the light of this world;
verses.11:10: yet if anyone walks in the night, he stumbles, for the light is not in him."
verses.11:11: He spoke these words, and afterward He said to them, "Lazarus our friend has fallen asleep; nevertheless, I am going that I may awaken him."
verses.11:12: So the disciples said to Him, "Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will be made well."
verses.11:13: Now Jesus had spoken concerning his death, yet they supposed that He was speaking of the rest of sleep.
verses.11:14: So then Jesus spoke plainly to them, "Lazarus has died,
verses.11:15: and for your sake I rejoice that I was not there, so that you may believe. Yet let us go to him."
verses.11:16: So Thomas, who was called Didymus, spoke to his fellow disciples, "Let us go as well, that we may die with Him."
verses.11:17: When Jesus came, therefore, He found that he had already been four days in the tomb.
verses.11:18: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.
verses.11:19: And many from among the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to comfort them over their brother.
verses.11:20: Therefore Martha, as soon as she heard that Jesus was coming, went to meet Him, while Mary remained sitting in the house.
verses.11:21: So Martha said to Jesus, "Lord, had You been here, my brother would not have died;
verses.11:22: and even now I know that whatever You ask of God, God will grant You."
verses.11:23: Jesus said to her, "Your brother shall rise again."
verses.11:24: Martha said to Him, "I know that he shall rise in the resurrection on the last day."
verses.11:25: Jesus said to her, "I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in Me, even if he dies, shall live,
verses.11:26: and everyone who lives and believes in Me shall by no means ever die. Do you believe this?"
verses.11:27: She said to Him, "Yes, Lord; I have come to believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, the One coming into the world."
verses.11:28: When she had spoken this, she departed and privately called her sister Mary, saying, "The Teacher is here, and He calls for you."
verses.11:29: And when she heard this, she rose up quickly and went toward Him.
verses.11:30: For Jesus had not yet arrived in the village, but remained still at the place where Martha had met Him.
verses.11:31: So the Jews who were with her in the house, comforting her, upon seeing that Mary rose swiftly and went out, followed after her, thinking that she was going to the tomb to weep there.
verses.11:32: Therefore, when Mary came to the place where Jesus was and saw Him, she fell at His feet, saying to Him, "Lord, had You been here, my brother would not have died."
verses.11:33: When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her weeping as well, He was deeply stirred in His spirit and troubled Himself,
verses.11:34: and He asked, "Where have you laid him?" They answered Him, "Lord, come and see."
verses.11:36: So the Jews were saying, "Behold, how He loved him!"
verses.11:37: But some among them said, "Could not this Man, who opened the eyes of the blind man, also have kept this one from dying?"
verses.11:38: Jesus, therefore, deeply stirred once more within Himself, came to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone was laid against it.
verses.11:39: Jesus said, "Remove the stone." Martha, the sister of the one who had died, said to Him, "Lord, by now there is a stench, for this is the fourth day."
verses.11:40: Jesus said to her, "Did I not tell you that if you believe, you shall see the glory of God?"
verses.11:41: So they removed the stone. And Jesus lifted His eyes upward and said, "Father, I thank You that You have heard Me,
verses.11:42: and I knew that You always hear Me; yet because of the multitude standing around I said this, so that they may believe that You sent Me."
verses.11:43: And when He had spoken these things, He cried out with a great voice, "Lazarus, come forth!"
verses.11:44: The one who had died came forth, his feet and hands bound with burial wrappings, and his face wrapped around with a cloth. Jesus said to them, "Loose him and let him depart."
verses.11:45: Therefore many of the Jews who had come to Mary and beheld the things He did believed in Him;
verses.11:46: but some among them departed to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
verses.11:47: So the chief priests and the Pharisees convened a council and were saying, "What are we to do? For this man is performing many signs.
verses.11:48: If we permit Him to go on like this, all will believe in Him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation."
verses.11:49: But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest of that year, said to them, "You know nothing whatever,
verses.11:50: nor do you consider that it is better for you that one man should die on behalf of the people, and that the entire nation should not perish."
verses.11:51: Now he did not say this of his own accord, but being high priest of that year, he prophesied that Jesus was about to die on behalf of the nation,
verses.11:52: and not on behalf of the nation alone, but also so that He might gather into one the children of God who are scattered abroad.
verses.11:53: Therefore, from that day forth, they took counsel that they might put Him to death.
verses.11:54: So Jesus no longer walked publicly among the Jews, but departed from there into the country near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim, and there He remained with the disciples.
verses.11:55: Now the Passover of the Jews was at hand, and many from the country went up to Jerusalem before the Passover to purify themselves.
verses.11:56: So they were looking for Jesus and speaking among themselves as they stood in the temple, "What do you suppose—that He will by no means come to the feast?"
verses.11:57: Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had issued commands that if anyone knew where He was, he should disclose it, so that they might seize Him.
verses.12:1: Therefore, six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus had raised from the dead.
verses.12:2: So they prepared a supper for Him there, and Martha served, while Lazarus was one of those who reclined at the table with Him.
verses.12:3: Then Mary took a pound of very costly ointment of pure spikenard, anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped His feet with her hair; and the house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.
verses.12:4: But Judas Iscariot, one of His disciples, who was about to betray Him, said,
verses.12:5: "Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?"
verses.12:6: Now he said this, not because he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief; and having the money box, he used to take what was put into it.
verses.12:7: Therefore Jesus said, "Leave her alone, that she may keep it for the day of My burial;
verses.12:8: for the poor you always have with you, but Me you do not always have."
verses.12:9: Then a great multitude of the Jews learned that He was there; and they came, not because of Jesus alone, but that they might also see Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.
verses.12:10: But the chief priests took counsel that they might put Lazarus to death also,
verses.12:11: because on account of him many of the Jews were going away and believing in Jesus.
verses.12:12: On the next day, the great multitude that had come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,
verses.12:13: took branches of palm trees and went out to meet Him, and cried aloud, "Hosanna! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord, even the King of Israel!"
verses.12:14: And Jesus, having found a young donkey, sat upon it, just as it is written:
verses.12:15: "Do not fear, daughter of Zion; behold, your King is coming, sitting on a donkey's colt."
verses.12:16: His disciples did not understand these things at first; but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things were written concerning Him and that they had done these things to Him.
verses.12:17: Therefore the multitude who had been with Him when He called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead bore witness.
verses.12:18: For this reason also the multitude met Him, because they had heard that He had performed this sign.
verses.12:19: So the Pharisees said among themselves, "You see that you accomplish nothing! Behold, the world has gone after Him!"
verses.12:20: Now there were certain Greeks among those who went up to worship at the feast.
verses.12:21: These, therefore, approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying, "Sir, we wish to see Jesus."
verses.12:22: Philip came and told Andrew, and Andrew and Philip came and told Jesus.
verses.12:23: But Jesus answered them, saying, "The hour has come that the Son of Man should be glorified.
verses.12:24: Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it abides alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
verses.12:25: He who loves his life loses it, and he who hates his life in this world shall keep it for eternal life.
verses.12:26: If anyone serves Me, let him follow Me; and where I am, there shall My servant be also. If anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.
verses.12:27: Now My soul is troubled, and what shall I say? Father, save Me from this hour! Yet for this purpose I came to this hour.
verses.12:28: Father, glorify Your name." Then a voice came from heaven: "I have both glorified it, and I will glorify it again."
verses.12:29: Therefore the multitude who stood by and heard it said that it had thundered; others said, "An angel has spoken to Him."
verses.12:30: Jesus answered and said, "This voice did not come for My sake, but for yours.
verses.12:31: Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world shall be cast out.
verses.12:32: And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all to Myself."
verses.12:33: Now He said this, signifying by what manner of death He was about to die.
verses.12:34: The multitude therefore answered Him, "We have heard from the Law that the Christ abides forever; and how do You say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?"
verses.12:35: Then Jesus said to them, "For a little while longer the light is among you. Walk while you have the light, lest darkness overtake you; and he who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
verses.12:36: While you have the light, believe in the light, that you may become sons of light." These things Jesus spoke, and departing, He hid Himself from them.
verses.12:37: Yet though He had performed so many signs before them, they did not believe in Him,
verses.12:38: so that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spoke: "Lord, who has believed our message, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?"
verses.12:39: For this reason they could not believe, because Isaiah said again:
verses.12:40: "He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, lest they should see with their eyes and understand with their heart and turn, and I would heal them."
verses.12:41: These things Isaiah said because he saw His glory and spoke concerning Him.
verses.12:42: Nevertheless, even among the rulers many believed in Him, but because of the Pharisees they did not confess it, lest they should be put out of the synagogue;
verses.12:43: for they loved the glory of men more than the glory of God.
verses.12:44: Then Jesus cried aloud and said, "He who believes in Me does not believe in Me, but in Him who sent Me.
verses.12:45: And he who beholds Me beholds Him who sent Me.
verses.12:46: I have come into the world as light, that everyone who believes in Me may not abide in the darkness.
verses.12:47: And if anyone hears My words and does not keep them, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
verses.12:48: He who rejects Me and does not receive My words has one who judges him—the word that I have spoken shall judge him on the last day.
verses.12:49: For I have not spoken from Myself; rather, the Father who sent Me has Himself given Me a commandment—what I should say and what I should speak.
verses.12:50: And I know that His commandment is eternal life. Therefore, the things that I speak, just as the Father has spoken to Me, so I speak."
verses.13:1: Now before the Feast of the Passover, Jesus, knowing that His hour had arrived to pass out of this world to the Father, having loved His own who were in the world, loved them to the very end.
verses.13:2: And while supper was taking place, the devil having already put it into the heart that Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon, should betray Him,
verses.13:3: Jesus, knowing that the Father had placed all things into His hands, and that He had come forth from God and was returning to God,
verses.13:4: arose from supper, laid aside His outer garments, and having taken a linen towel, girded Himself.
verses.13:5: Then He poured water into the basin and began to wash the feet of the disciples, and to wipe them dry with the towel with which He was girded.
verses.13:6: So He came to Simon Peter, and Peter said to Him, "Lord, are You washing my feet?"
verses.13:7: Jesus answered and said to him, "What I am doing you do not know now, yet you shall understand after these things."
verses.13:8: Peter said to Him, "By no means shall You ever wash my feet!" Jesus answered him, "Unless I wash you, you have no portion with Me."
verses.13:9: Simon Peter said to Him, "Lord, not my feet alone, but also my hands and my head!"
verses.13:10: Jesus said to him, "The one who has bathed has no need except to wash his feet, but is wholly clean; and you are clean, yet not all of you."
verses.13:11: For He knew who was betraying Him; because of this He said, "Not all of you are clean."
verses.13:12: So when He had washed their feet, taken His outer garments, and reclined at table, He spoke to them again, "Do you understand what I have done to you?
verses.13:13: You address Me as 'Teacher' and 'Lord,' and you speak rightly, for so I am.
verses.13:14: Therefore, if I, the Lord and the Teacher, washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.
verses.13:15: For I have set an example for you, that just as I have done to you, you also should do.
verses.13:16: Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, a servant is not greater than his master, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him.
verses.13:17: If you know these things, blessed are you if you practice them.
verses.13:18: I do not speak concerning all of you; I know those whom I have chosen. Yet it is that the Scripture may be fulfilled, 'He who eats bread with Me has lifted up his heel against Me.'
verses.13:19: From now on I am telling you before it comes to pass, that when it comes to pass, you may believe that I am.
verses.13:20: Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, whoever receives anyone I send receives Me; and whoever receives Me receives Him who sent Me."
verses.13:21: Having spoken these things, Jesus was troubled in spirit, and testified and said, "Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you that one of you shall betray Me."
verses.13:22: The disciples looked at one another, at a loss to know of whom He was speaking.
verses.13:23: Now one of His disciples, the one whom Jesus loved, was reclining in the bosom of Jesus.
verses.13:24: So Simon Peter motioned to him to inquire who it might be of whom He was speaking.
verses.13:25: Then, leaning back thus upon the breast of Jesus, he said to Him, "Lord, who is it?"
verses.13:26: Jesus answered, "He is the one to whom I will give the morsel once I dip it." Then, having dipped the morsel, He gave it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot.
verses.13:27: And after the morsel, Satan then entered into him. Therefore Jesus said to him, "What you are doing, do swiftly."
verses.13:28: Yet none of those reclining at the table knew why He spoke this to him.
verses.13:29: For some supposed, since Judas kept the money box, that Jesus was saying to him, "Purchase what we need for the feast," or that he should give something to the poor.
verses.13:30: So after receiving the morsel, he went out immediately; and it was night.
verses.13:31: Therefore, when he had gone out, Jesus said, "Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in Him.
verses.13:32: And God shall glorify Him in Himself, and immediately He shall glorify Him.
verses.13:33: Little children, yet a little while I am with you. You shall seek Me; and just as I declared to the Jews, 'Where I go you cannot come,' so now I say to you also.
verses.13:34: A new commandment I give you, that you love one another: just as I loved you, that you likewise love one another.
verses.13:35: In this all shall know that you are My disciples, if you have love one toward another."
verses.13:36: Simon Peter said to Him, "Lord, where are You going?" Jesus answered him, "Where I go you cannot follow Me now, yet afterward you shall follow."
verses.13:37: Peter said to Him, "Lord, why can I not follow You at this time? I will lay down my life for You."
verses.13:38: Jesus answered, "Will you lay down your life for Me? Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, a rooster shall by no means crow until you have denied Me three times."
verses.14:1: "Do not let your heart be troubled; believe in God, and believe in Me also.
verses.14:2: In the house of My Father there are many abodes; if it were not so, I would have told you, for I am going to prepare a place for you.
verses.14:3: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I am coming again and shall take you to Myself, that where I am, you also may be.
verses.14:4: And where I am going, you know the way."
verses.14:5: Thomas said to Him, "Lord, we do not know where You are going; how are we able to know the way?"
verses.14:6: Jesus said to him, "I am the way, and the truth, and the life; none comes to the Father except through Me.
verses.14:7: If you had known Me, you would also have known My Father; from now on you know Him and have seen Him."
verses.14:8: Philip said to Him, "Lord, show us the Father, and it suffices us."
verses.14:9: Jesus said to him, "For so long a time I have been with you, and have you not come to know Me, Philip? Whoever has seen Me has seen the Father; how is it that you say, 'Show us the Father'?
verses.14:10: Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in Me? The words which I speak to you I do not speak from Myself; rather, the Father who abides in Me performs His works.
verses.14:11: Believe Me that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me; otherwise, believe because of the works themselves.
verses.14:12: Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, he who believes in Me shall also do the works that I do, and greater works than these he shall do, because I am going to the Father.
verses.14:13: And whatever you may ask in My name, this I shall do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
verses.14:14: If you ask Me anything in My name, I Myself shall do it.
verses.14:15: If you love Me, you shall keep My commandments.
verses.14:16: And I will ask the Father, and He shall give you another Comforter, that He may be with you forever—
verses.14:17: the Spirit of truth, whom the world is unable to receive, because it neither beholds Him nor knows Him; you know Him, for He abides with you and shall be in you.
verses.14:18: I shall not leave you as orphans; I am coming to you.
verses.14:19: Yet a little while and the world beholds Me no more, but you behold Me; because I live, you also shall live.
verses.14:20: On that day you yourselves shall know that I am in My Father, and you are in Me, and I am in you.
verses.14:21: Whoever has My commandments and keeps them, that is the one who loves Me; and the one who loves Me shall be loved by My Father, and I shall love him and manifest Myself to him."
verses.14:22: Judas—not Iscariot—said to Him, "Lord, what has come to pass that You are about to manifest Yourself to us and not to the world?"
verses.14:23: Jesus answered and said to him, "If anyone loves Me, he shall keep My word; and My Father shall love him, and We shall come to him and make Our abode with him.
