verses.14:24: Whoever does not love Me does not keep My words; and the word that you are hearing is not Mine, but belongs to the Father who sent Me.
verses.14:25: I have spoken these things to you while abiding with you.
verses.14:26: Yet the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father shall send in My name—He shall teach you all things and remind you of everything that I told you.
verses.14:27: Peace I leave with you; My own peace I give to you; not in the way the world gives do I give to you. Do not let your heart be troubled, nor let it be fainthearted.
verses.14:28: You heard that I told you, 'I am going away and am coming to you.' If you loved Me, you would have rejoiced because I am going to the Father, for the Father is greater than I.
verses.14:29: And now I have spoken to you before it happens, that when it comes to pass, you may believe.
verses.14:30: I shall not speak much longer with you, for the ruler of the world is coming, and in Me he has nothing;
verses.14:31: rather, it is so that the world may know that I love the Father, and just as the Father has commanded Me, so I do. Arise, let us depart from here."
verses.15:1: "I am the true vine, and My Father is the vineyard keeper.
verses.15:2: Every branch in Me that bears no fruit He removes, and every branch that bears fruit He prunes, so that it may bear more fruit.
verses.15:3: Already you are clean on account of the word that I have spoken to you.
verses.15:4: Abide in Me, and I in you. Just as the branch is unable to bear fruit of itself unless it abides in the vine, so neither can you unless you abide in Me.
verses.15:5: I am the vine; you are the branches. The one who abides in Me, and I in him, he bears much fruit; for apart from Me you are able to do nothing.
verses.15:6: If anyone does not abide in Me, he is cast forth like the branch and withers; and they gather them and throw them into the fire, and they are burned.
verses.15:7: If you abide in Me, and My words abide in you, ask for whatever you desire, and it shall be done for you.
verses.15:8: In this My Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit and become My disciples.
verses.15:9: Just as the Father has loved Me, I also have loved you; abide in My love.
verses.15:10: If you keep My commandments, you shall abide in My love, even as I have kept the Father's commandments and abide in His love.
verses.15:11: These things I have spoken to you, so that My joy may be in you, and your joy may be made full.
verses.15:12: This is My commandment: that you love one another, even as I have loved you.
verses.15:13: No one has greater love than this: that one should lay down his life for his friends.
verses.15:14: You are My friends if you do the things that I command you.
verses.15:15: I no longer call you servants, because the servant does not know what his master is doing; rather, I have called you friends, because all that I heard from My Father I have made known to you.
verses.15:16: It was not you who chose Me, but I who chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should abide, so that whatever you ask the Father in My name He may give to you.
verses.15:17: These things I command you, so that you may love one another.
verses.15:18: If the world hates you, know that it has hated Me before you.
verses.15:19: If you were of the world, the world would love what is its own; yet because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, for this reason the world hates you.
verses.15:20: Remember the word that I spoke to you: 'A servant is not greater than his master.' If they persecuted Me, they will persecute you as well; if they kept My word, they will keep yours as well.
verses.15:21: Yet all these things they will do against you on account of My name, because they do not know the One who sent Me.
verses.15:22: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would have had no sin; yet now they have no excuse for their sin.
verses.15:23: He who hates Me also hates My Father.
verses.15:24: If I had not done among them the works that no one else has done, they would have had no sin; yet now they have both seen and hated both Me and My Father.
verses.15:25: Yet this is so that the word written in their law might be fulfilled: 'They hated Me without cause.'
verses.15:26: When the Advocate comes, whom I shall send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father—He shall bear witness concerning Me.
verses.15:27: And you also bear witness, because you have been with Me from the beginning."
verses.16:1: "These things I have spoken to you, lest you be caused to stumble.
verses.16:2: They will expel you from the synagogues; indeed, an hour is coming when everyone who kills you will suppose that he is offering sacred service to God.
verses.16:3: And they will do these things because they have known neither the Father nor Me.
verses.16:4: Yet I have spoken these things to you, so that when their hour comes you may remember them, that I Myself told you. Now I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you.
verses.16:5: But now I am going to the One who sent Me, and not one of you asks Me, 'Where are You going?'
verses.16:6: Rather, because I have spoken these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart.
verses.16:7: Yet I tell you the truth: it is for your benefit that I go away; for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I depart, I shall send Him to you.
verses.16:8: And when He comes, He will convict the world concerning sin, and concerning righteousness, and concerning judgment:
verses.16:9: concerning sin, because they do not believe in Me;
verses.16:10: concerning righteousness, because I go to the Father and you no longer behold Me;
verses.16:11: and concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
verses.16:12: I still have many things to speak to you, yet you are not able to bear them at this time.
verses.16:13: Yet when He comes, the Spirit of truth, He will guide you into all the truth; for He will not speak from Himself, but whatever He shall hear He will speak, and He will declare to you the things that are to come.
verses.16:14: He will glorify Me, because He will receive from what is Mine and will declare it to you.
verses.16:15: All things that the Father has are Mine; for this reason I said that He receives from what is Mine and will declare it to you.
verses.16:16: A little while, and you no longer behold Me; and again a little while, and you shall see Me."
verses.16:17: Therefore some of His disciples said to one another, "What is this that He says to us: 'A little while, and you do not behold Me; and again a little while, and you shall see Me'; and, 'Because I go to the Father'?"
verses.16:18: So they were saying, "What is this that He says, 'a little while'? We do not know what He is speaking of."
verses.16:19: Jesus knew that they desired to question Him, and He said to them, "Are you inquiring among yourselves about this, that I said, 'A little while, and you do not behold Me; and again a little while, and you shall see Me'?
verses.16:20: Assuredly, I say to you that you will weep and lament, while the world will rejoice; you will be made sorrowful, yet your sorrow shall become joy.
verses.16:21: A woman, when she is giving birth, has sorrow because her hour has come; yet when she has delivered the child, she no longer remembers the anguish, on account of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.
verses.16:22: Therefore you also now have sorrow; yet I shall see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you.
verses.16:23: And in that day you will question Me about nothing. Assuredly, I say to you, if you ask the Father for anything, He will give it to you in My name.
verses.16:24: Until this time you have asked for nothing in My name; ask, and you shall receive, so that your joy may be made full.
verses.16:25: These things I have spoken to you in figures of speech; an hour is coming when I shall no longer speak to you in figures of speech, but shall declare to you plainly concerning the Father.
verses.16:26: In that day you will ask in My name, and I do not say to you that I shall petition the Father on your behalf;
verses.16:27: for the Father Himself loves you, because you yourselves have loved Me and have believed that I came forth from God.
verses.16:28: I came forth from the Father and have come into the world; again, I am leaving the world and departing to the Father."
verses.16:29: His disciples say, "Behold, now You speak plainly, and You speak no figure of speech.
verses.16:30: Now we know that You know all things and have no need for anyone to question You; by this we believe that You came forth from God."
verses.16:31: Jesus answered them, "Do you believe now?
verses.16:32: Behold, an hour is coming, and indeed has come, when you will be scattered, each to his own home, and will leave Me alone; yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.
verses.16:33: These things I have spoken to you, so that in Me you may have peace. In the world you have tribulation; yet be of good courage—I have overcome the world."
verses.17:1: These things Jesus spoke, and lifting His eyes toward heaven, He said, "Father, the hour has come; glorify Your Son, so that the Son may glorify You,
verses.17:2: even as You gave Him authority over all flesh, that to all whom You have given Him, He should give eternal life.
verses.17:3: Now this is eternal life: that they may know You, the only true God, and Him whom You sent, Jesus Christ.
verses.17:4: I glorified You upon the earth, having completed the work which You have given Me to do.
verses.17:5: And now, Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory which I had beside You before the world existed.
verses.17:6: I have made Your name manifest to the men whom You gave Me out of the world. Yours they were, and to Me You gave them, and they have kept Your word.
verses.17:7: Now they have come to know that all things which You have given Me are from You,
verses.17:8: for the words which You gave Me I have given to them; and they received them and truly knew that I came forth from You, and they believed that You sent Me.
verses.17:9: I pray on their behalf; I do not pray for the world, but for those whom You have given Me, because they are Yours,
verses.17:10: and all things that are Mine are Yours, and Yours are Mine, and I have been glorified in them.
verses.17:11: And I am no longer in the world, yet they are in the world, and I am coming to You. Holy Father, keep them in Your name which You have given Me, that they may be one, even as We are.
verses.17:12: While I was with them, I kept them in Your name which You have given Me, and I guarded them; and not one of them perished except the son of perdition, that the Scripture might be fulfilled.
verses.17:13: Yet now I am coming to You, and these things I speak in the world, so that they may have My joy made full within themselves.
verses.17:14: I have given Your word to them, and the world hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
verses.17:15: I do not pray that You take them away from the world, but that You keep them from the evil one.
verses.17:16: Of the world they are not, even as I am not of the world.
verses.17:17: Consecrate them in the truth; Your word is truth.
verses.17:18: Even as You sent Me into the world, I also sent them into the world.
verses.17:19: And on their behalf I consecrate Myself, so that they themselves also may be consecrated in truth.
verses.17:20: Yet I do not pray for these alone, but also for those who believe in Me through their word,
verses.17:21: that all of them may be one, even as You, Father, are in Me and I in You, that they also may be in Us, in order that the world may believe that You sent Me.
verses.17:22: And the glory which You have given Me I have given to them, so that they may be one, even as We are one:
verses.17:23: I in them, and You in Me, that they may be perfected into one, so that the world may know that You sent Me and loved them even as You loved Me.
verses.17:24: Father, as for those whom You have given Me, I desire that where I am, they also may be with Me, so that they may behold My glory which You have given Me, because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.
verses.17:25: Righteous Father, even though the world did not know You, yet I knew You, and these knew that You sent Me;
verses.17:26: and I have made Your name known to them, and will make it known, so that the love with which You loved Me may be in them, and I in them."
verses.18:1: Having spoken these things, Jesus went forth with His disciples across the brook Kidron, where there was a garden, into which He and His disciples entered.
verses.18:2: Now Judas also, who was betraying Him, knew the place, because Jesus had often gathered there with His disciples.
verses.18:3: So Judas, having taken the cohort of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and from the Pharisees, came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.
verses.18:4: Jesus therefore, knowing all the things that were coming upon Him, went forth and said to them, "Whom do you seek?"
verses.18:5: They answered Him, "Jesus the Nazarene." He said to them, "I am He." And Judas also, who was betraying Him, was standing with them.
verses.18:6: Therefore, when He said to them, "I am He," they stepped back and fell to the ground.
verses.18:7: Again therefore He questioned them, "Whom do you seek?" And they said, "Jesus the Nazarene."
verses.18:8: Jesus answered, "I told you that I am He; if therefore you seek Me, let these men go,"
verses.18:9: so that the word might be fulfilled which He spoke: "Of those whom You have given Me, I did not lose a single one."
verses.18:10: Then Simon Peter, who had a sword, drew it, struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear. Now the servant's name was Malchus.
verses.18:11: Therefore Jesus said to Peter, "Put the sword into its sheath. The cup which the Father has given Me, shall I not drink it?"
verses.18:12: Then the cohort of soldiers and the commander and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus and bound Him,
verses.18:13: and led Him first to Annas; for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
verses.18:14: Now Caiaphas was the one who had counseled the Jews that it was expedient for one man to die on behalf of the people.
verses.18:15: And Simon Peter was following Jesus, along with another disciple. Now that disciple was known to the high priest, and he entered with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest;
verses.18:16: but Peter stood outside at the door. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought Peter inside.
verses.18:17: Then the servant girl who kept the door said to Peter, "Surely you also are not one of this man's disciples?" He replied, "I am not."
verses.18:18: Now the servants and the officers were standing there, having made a charcoal fire because it was cold, and they were warming themselves; and Peter also was standing with them, warming himself.
verses.18:19: Then the high priest questioned Jesus concerning His disciples and concerning His teaching.
verses.18:20: Jesus answered him, "I have spoken openly to the world. I always taught in synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews gather together, and in secret I spoke nothing.
verses.18:21: Why do you question Me? Question those who have heard what I spoke to them; behold, these know the things which I said."
verses.18:22: Now when He had spoken these things, one of the officers standing by struck Jesus with his hand, saying, "Is this how You answer the high priest?"
verses.18:23: Jesus answered him, "If I spoke wrongly, bear witness to the wrong; yet if rightly, why do you strike Me?"
verses.18:24: Annas therefore sent Him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.
verses.18:25: Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. So they said to him, "Surely you also are not one of His disciples?" He denied it and said, "I am not."
verses.18:26: One of the high priest's servants, being a kinsman of the one whose ear Peter had cut off, said, "Did I not see you with Him in the garden?"
verses.18:27: Therefore Peter denied it again, and at once a rooster crowed.
verses.18:28: Then they brought Jesus from Caiaphas into the Praetorium; and it was early morning. Yet they themselves did not enter the Praetorium, lest they be defiled, but rather might eat the Passover.
verses.18:29: Therefore Pilate went outside to them and said, "What accusation do you bring against this man?"
verses.18:30: They answered and said to him, "If this man were not doing evil, we would not have delivered Him over to you."
verses.18:31: Therefore Pilate said to them, "Take Him yourselves, and according to your law judge Him." The Jews said to him, "It is not permitted for us to put anyone to death,"
verses.18:32: so that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled which He spoke, indicating by what kind of death He was about to die.
verses.18:33: Then Pilate entered the Praetorium again, summoned Jesus, and said to Him, "Are You the King of the Jews?"
verses.18:34: Jesus answered, "Do you say this of your own accord, or did others tell you concerning Me?"
verses.18:35: Pilate answered, "Am I a Jew? Your own nation and the chief priests delivered You over to me. What have You done?"
verses.18:36: Jesus answered, "My kingdom is not of this world. If My kingdom were of this world, My servants would be fighting, lest I be delivered over to the Jews; yet as it is, My kingdom is not from here."
verses.18:37: Therefore Pilate said to Him, "Then You are a king?" Jesus answered, "You say that I am a king. To this end I have been born, and to this end I have come into the world, that I may bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears My voice."
verses.18:38: Pilate said to Him, "What is truth?" And having said this, he went out again to the Jews and said to them, "I find no grounds for a charge in Him.
verses.18:39: Yet you have a custom that I should release one man to you at the Passover; do you wish therefore that I release to you the King of the Jews?"
verses.18:40: Therefore they cried out again, saying, "Not this man, but Barabbas!" Now Barabbas was a robber.
verses.19:1: So Pilate then took Jesus and scourged Him.
verses.19:2: And the soldiers wove a crown of thorns and placed it upon His head, and clothed Him in a purple robe,
verses.19:3: and they kept coming up to Him and saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!" and kept striking Him with their hands.
verses.19:4: And Pilate went out again and said to them, "Behold, I bring Him out to you, so that you may know that I find no fault at all in Him."
verses.19:5: Jesus therefore came outside, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe; and he said to them, "Behold, the Man!"
verses.19:6: When the chief priests and the officers saw Him, therefore, they shouted, saying, "Crucify! Crucify!" Pilate said to them, "Take Him yourselves and crucify Him, for I myself find no fault in Him."
verses.19:7: The Jews answered him, "We have a law, and according to the law He must die, because He made Himself the Son of God."
verses.19:8: So when Pilate heard this word, he feared all the more,
verses.19:9: and he entered into the Praetorium again and said to Jesus, "Where are You from?" Yet Jesus did not give him an answer.
verses.19:10: Therefore Pilate said to Him, "Do You not speak to me? Do You not know that I have authority to release You, and I have authority to crucify You?"
verses.19:11: Jesus answered him, "You would have no authority against Me at all unless it had been given to you from above; because of this, the one who delivered Me to you has greater sin."
verses.19:12: From that moment Pilate was seeking to release Him, but the Jews shouted, saying, "If you release this Man, you are not a friend of Caesar; everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar."
verses.19:13: Having heard these words, Pilate therefore led Jesus outside and took his seat upon the judgment seat, at a place called the Stone Pavement—but in Hebrew, Gabbatha.
verses.19:14: Now it was the Preparation of the Passover; it was about the sixth hour. And he said to the Jews, "Behold, your King!"
verses.19:15: Then they shouted, "Take Him away! Take Him away! Crucify Him!" Pilate said to them, "Shall I crucify your King?" The chief priests answered, "We have no king except Caesar."
verses.19:16: So then he delivered Him to them that He might be crucified. And they took Jesus;
verses.19:17: and carrying the cross for Himself, He went out to the place called the Place of a Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha,
verses.19:18: where they crucified Him, and with Him two others, one on this side and one on that, with Jesus in the midst.
verses.19:19: Now Pilate also wrote a title and placed it upon the cross, and it was written, "Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the Jews."
verses.19:20: Therefore many of the Jews read this title, because the place where Jesus was crucified was close to the city; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.
verses.19:21: So the chief priests of the Jews were saying to Pilate, "Do not write, 'The King of the Jews,' but rather that He said, 'I am King of the Jews.'"
verses.19:22: Pilate replied, "That which I have written, I have written."
verses.19:23: The soldiers therefore, when they had crucified Jesus, took His garments and made four shares, a share for each soldier, and also the tunic. Now the tunic was seamless, woven from the top throughout.
verses.19:24: Therefore they said to one another, "Let us not tear it, but let us draw lots for it, whose it shall be," so that the Scripture might be fulfilled which says, "They divided My garments among themselves, and for My vesture they cast a lot." Thus the soldiers did these things.
verses.19:25: Now beside the cross of Jesus stood His mother and the sister of His mother, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
verses.19:26: Therefore Jesus, seeing His mother and the disciple whom He loved standing nearby, said to His mother, "Woman, behold, your son!"
verses.19:27: Next He said to the disciple, "Behold, your mother!" And from that hour the disciple received her into his own home.
verses.19:28: After this, Jesus, knowing that all things had now been accomplished, in order that the Scripture might be fulfilled, said, "I thirst."
verses.19:29: A vessel full of sour wine was set there; therefore they put a sponge full of the sour wine upon hyssop and brought it to His mouth.
verses.19:30: When Jesus therefore had received the sour wine, He said, "It is finished!" And bowing His head, He yielded up His spirit.
verses.19:31: Therefore the Jews, since it was the Preparation, so that the bodies would not remain upon the cross on the Sabbath—for the day of that Sabbath was a high day—asked Pilate that their legs might be broken and that they might be taken away.
verses.19:32: So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first, and of the other who had been crucified with Him;
verses.19:33: but upon coming to Jesus, when they saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs;
verses.19:34: rather, one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came forth.
verses.19:35: And he who has seen it has borne witness, and his testimony is true; and he knows that he speaks the truth, so that you also may believe.
verses.19:36: For these things came to pass so that the Scripture might be fulfilled, "Not a bone of Him shall be broken."
verses.19:37: And once more another Scripture says, "They shall look upon Him whom they pierced."
verses.19:38: Now after these things, Joseph of Arimathea—being a disciple of Jesus, though secretly because of fear of the Jews—asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus; and Pilate granted permission. He came therefore and took away His body.
verses.19:39: And Nicodemus also came—the one who at the first had come to Him by night—bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about one hundred pounds.
verses.19:40: Therefore they took the body of Jesus and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as is the custom among the Jews to prepare for burial.
verses.19:41: Now in the place where He had been crucified was a garden, and in that garden a new tomb, in which no one had as yet been laid.
verses.19:42: There, therefore, because of the Preparation of the Jews—since the tomb was close at hand—they laid Jesus.
verses.20:1: Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene came early to the tomb while darkness still remained, and saw the stone removed from the tomb.
verses.20:2: Therefore she ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple, the one whom Jesus loved, and said to them, "They have taken the Lord from the tomb, and we do not know where they have laid Him."
verses.20:3: Peter therefore went forth, and the other disciple, and they were going to the tomb.
verses.20:4: And the two were running together; and the other disciple ran ahead more swiftly than Peter and arrived at the tomb first.
verses.20:5: And stooping down to look inside, he saw the linen wrappings lying there; yet he did not enter.
verses.20:6: Therefore Simon Peter also came, following after him, and entered the tomb; and he beheld the linen wrappings lying there,
verses.20:7: and the face cloth that had been upon His head, not lying with the linen wrappings, but folded up apart in a place of its own.
verses.20:8: Then the other disciple, who had come to the tomb first, entered also, and he saw and believed.
verses.20:9: For they did not yet understand the Scripture, that it was necessary for Him to rise from the dead.
verses.20:10: Therefore the disciples departed again to their own homes.
verses.20:11: But Mary was standing outside at the tomb, weeping. So as she wept, she stooped down to look inside the tomb,
verses.20:12: and she beheld two angels in white seated there, one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.
verses.20:13: And they said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping?" She replied to them, "They have removed my Lord, and I do not know where they have laid Him."
verses.20:14: When she had spoken these words, she turned around and beheld Jesus standing there, and she did not know that it was Jesus.
verses.20:15: Jesus said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping? Whom do you seek?" She, supposing that He was the gardener, said to Him, "Sir, if You have borne Him away, tell me where You have placed Him, and I will take Him away."
verses.20:16: Jesus said to her, "Mary!" Turning, she said to Him in Hebrew, "Rabboni!" (which means Teacher).
verses.20:17: Jesus said to her, "Do not cling to Me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father; rather, go to My brethren and tell them, 'I am ascending to My Father and your Father, and to My God and your God.'"
verses.20:18: Mary Magdalene came bringing word to the disciples, "I have seen the Lord," and that He had said these things to her.
verses.20:19: Therefore, when it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors were locked where the disciples were because of fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in their midst, and said to them, "Peace be to you."
verses.20:20: And when He had said this, He showed His hands and His side to them. Therefore the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
verses.20:21: Jesus therefore said to them again, "Peace be to you; just as the Father has sent Me, I also am sending you."
verses.20:22: And having said this, He breathed upon them and said to them, "Receive the Holy Spirit.
verses.20:23: If you forgive the sins of any, they stand forgiven to them; if you retain the sins of any, they stand retained."
verses.20:24: Now Thomas, one of the twelve, the one called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
verses.20:25: Therefore the other disciples were saying to him, "We have seen the Lord." Yet he said to them, "Unless I see in His hands the imprint of the nails, and place my finger into the imprint of the nails, and place my hand into His side, I will by no means believe."
verses.20:26: And after eight days His disciples were inside once again, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came while the doors were locked, and stood in their midst and said, "Peace be to you."
verses.20:27: Next He said to Thomas, "Bring your finger here and behold My hands; and bring your hand and place it into My side; and do not become unbelieving, but believing."
verses.20:28: Thomas replied and said to Him, "My Lord and my God!"
verses.20:29: Jesus said to him, "Because you have seen Me, have you believed? Blessed are those who did not see, and yet believed."
verses.20:30: Indeed, Jesus also performed many other signs before His disciples, which are not written in this book;
verses.20:31: yet these things have been written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that through believing you may have life in His name.
verses.21:1: After these things Jesus manifested Himself again to the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias; and He manifested Himself in this way.
verses.21:2: There were together Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael from Cana of Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two others from among His disciples.
verses.21:3: Simon Peter said to them, "I am going fishing." They replied to him, "We also are coming with you." They went forth and entered the boat, and in that night they caught nothing.
verses.21:4: Now when daybreak had already come, Jesus stood upon the shore; however, the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.
verses.21:5: Therefore Jesus said to them, "Children, do you have any fish at all?" They replied to Him, "No."
verses.21:6: And He said to them, "Cast the net upon the right side of the boat, and you shall find some." Therefore they cast it, and they were no longer able to haul it in on account of the multitude of fish.
verses.21:7: Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, "It is the Lord!" When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girded his outer garment around himself, for he was naked, and cast himself into the sea.
verses.21:8: But the other disciples came in the small boat, for they were not far from the land, only about two hundred cubits away, dragging the net of fish.
verses.21:9: Therefore, when they had stepped out onto the land, they saw a charcoal fire laid there, and fish lying upon it, and bread.
verses.21:10: Jesus said to them, "Bring here some of the fish that you have just now caught."
verses.21:11: So Simon Peter went aboard and hauled the net onto the land, full of large fish, one hundred fifty-three; and even though there were so many, the net was not torn.
verses.21:12: Jesus said to them, "Come, eat the morning meal." Yet not one of the disciples dared to inquire of Him, "Who are You?" knowing that it was the Lord.
verses.21:13: Jesus came, took the bread, and gave it to them, and the fish in the same manner.
verses.21:14: This was now the third time Jesus was manifested to the disciples after He had been raised from the dead.
verses.21:15: Therefore, when they had finished the morning meal, Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Simon, son of John, do you love Me more than these?" He replied to Him, "Yes, Lord, You know that I love You." He said to him, "Feed My lambs."
verses.21:16: He spoke to him again, a second time, "Simon, son of John, do you love Me?" He answered Him, "Yes, Lord, You know that I love You." He said to him, "Shepherd My sheep."
verses.21:17: He said to him the third time, "Simon, son of John, do you love Me?" Peter became grieved because He had said to him the third time, "Do you love Me?" And he replied to Him, "Lord, You know everything; You know that I love You." Jesus said to him, "Feed My sheep.
verses.21:18: Assuredly, assuredly, I say to you, when you were younger, you girded yourself and walked wherever you desired; yet when you grow old, you shall stretch forth your hands, and another shall gird you and carry you where you do not desire."
verses.21:19: Now this He said to signify by what manner of death he would glorify God. And having spoken this, He said to him, "Follow Me."
verses.21:20: Turning around, Peter saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following—the one who at the supper had also leaned back upon His breast and said, "Lord, who is the one betraying You?"
verses.21:21: Therefore, seeing him, Peter said to Jesus, "Lord, and what of this man?"
verses.21:22: Jesus said to him, "If I wish that he abide until I come, what is that to you? As for you, follow Me."
verses.21:23: Therefore this saying went forth among the brethren: that disciple would not die. Yet Jesus did not say to him that he would not die, but rather, "If I wish that he abide until I come, what is that to you?"
verses.21:24: This is the disciple who bears witness concerning these things, and who has written these things; and we know that his witness is true.
verses.21:25: Yet there are also many other things that Jesus did; if they were written down one by one, I suppose that not even the world itself could hold the books that would be written.

notes.1:1: In Greek, theos en ho logos fronts the anarthrous predicate noun theos to affirm the Word's full deity without confounding His person with the Father; pros ton theon expresses personal communion ('with God').
notes.1:3: Following the punctuation of the Saints Greek Critical Text, ho gegonen ('That which has come into being') opens verse 4; other editions place the stop after it at the end of verse 3. In v. 5 katelaben carries a double nuance of 'overcame' and 'comprehended.'
notes.1:14: Greek eskenosen literally means 'pitched His tent / tabernacled,' evoking God's dwelling presence in the tabernacle of Exodus.
notes.1:18: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads monogenes theos ('the only-begotten God,' supported by P66, P75, Sinaiticus, and Vaticanus), whereas later manuscripts read 'the only-begotten Son.'
notes.1:51: Although Jesus speaks directly to Nathanael ('to him'), the Greek shifts from second-person singular (v. 50) to second-person plural ('to you, you shall see'), encompassing all the disciples.
notes.2:4: Literally "What is it to Me and to you, woman?"—a Semitic idiom signaling gentle distance rather than disrespect, as "woman" (Greek gynai) was a polite form of address.
notes.2:6: A "measure" (Greek metretes) was a liquid measure of roughly nine to ten gallons (about thirty-nine liters), meaning each stone jar held about twenty to thirty gallons.
notes.2:17: Quoting Psalm 69:9 (LXX 68:10); the critical Greek text reads the future tense "will devour Me," whereas later manuscripts harmonize to the past tense "has eaten Me up."
notes.2:24: The Greek uses the same verb (pisteuo) for the crowd's "believed" in verse 23 and Jesus' refusal to "entrust" Himself to them here, highlighting the contrast between superficial faith and true trust.
notes.3:3: The Greek adverb anothen carries a deliberate double meaning—"anew/again" and "from above"—which explains Nicodemus' literal misunderstanding in verse 4 while anticipating "from above" in verse 31.
notes.3:13: The earliest Greek manuscripts end the verse with "the Son of Man"; later manuscripts add the clause "who is in heaven."
notes.3:16: Greek monogenes denotes "only begotten" or "unique, one of a kind." Because ancient Greek manuscripts lack quotation marks, interpreters differ on whether verses 16-21 continue Jesus' words to Nicodemus or provide the evangelist's reflection.
notes.3:25: The critical Greek text reads the singular "a Jew," whereas later manuscripts read the plural "the Jews."
notes.3:31: Many interpreters treat verses 31-36 as the evangelist's theological reflection following John the Baptist's climactic words in verse 30, though others view them as a continuation of John's testimony.
notes.4:9: The Greek verb συγχρῶνται can mean either 'associate with' or more specifically 'use vessels in common with,' reflecting Jewish purity customs concerning Samaritans.
notes.4:26: Literally 'I am, the One speaking to you' (Ἐγώ εἰμι); while serving as a direct self-identification as the Messiah, the wording also echoes the solemn divine self-revelation of Exodus 3:14 and Isaiah 43:10 and 52:6.
notes.4:35: In the critical Greek text, the adverb ἤδη ('Already') stands after the pause at the end of verse 35 and introduces the sentence continuing into verse 36, whereas older editions attach it to the preceding clause ('already white for harvest').
notes.4:42: The earliest Greek manuscripts read simply 'the Savior of the world,' without the additional title 'the Christ' found in later Byzantine witnesses.
notes.4:46: The Greek term βασιλικός denotes an officer in royal service, most likely an official attached to the court of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee.
notes.5:2: The Greek critical text reads Bethzatha (rather than Bethesda), and the feminine adjective for "Sheep" is traditionally understood to imply the Sheep Gate.
notes.5:3: The earliest Greek manuscripts conclude verse 3 at "withered" and omit the explanation of an angel stirring the water found in later manuscripts as the end of verse 3 and verse 4.
notes.5:27: In Greek "Son of Man" appears here without the definite article, echoing Daniel 7:13 and underscoring Christ's messianic authority to execute judgment.
notes.5:39: The Greek verb form can be taken either as an indicative ("You search," fitting the surrounding argument in verses 39-40) or as an imperative ("Search").
notes.6:11: The Greek critical text states directly that Jesus distributed the loaves to those reclining, without the later manuscript expansion adding 'to the disciples, and the disciples to those reclining.'
notes.6:19: Twenty-five to thirty stadia equals roughly three to three and a half miles (about five kilometers), placing the boat well out toward the middle of the Sea of Galilee.
notes.6:20: The Greek phrase 'Ego eimi' serves immediately as a word of recognition ('It is I'), while also carrying the solemn Johannine resonance of the divine self-revelation ('I am'; cf. Exodus 3:14).
notes.6:33: The Greek masculine participle 'ho katabainon' agrees grammatically with both 'bread' ('that which descends') and a person ('He who descends'), preparing for Jesus's explicit declaration in verse 35.
notes.6:47: The Greek critical text reads simply 'the one who believes has eternal life,' without the later manuscript addition 'in Me.'
notes.6:51: The Greek critical text ends with 'is My flesh, for the life of the world,' omitting the repeated clause 'which I will give' found in later manuscripts.
notes.6:55: The Greek critical text uses the adjective 'alethes' ('true food ... true drink') rather than the later adverbial variant 'alethos' ('food indeed ... drink indeed').
notes.6:69: The Greek critical text reads 'the Holy One of God,' whereas later Byzantine manuscripts expand Peter's confession toward Matthew 16:16 ('the Christ, the Son of the living God').
notes.7:8: The Greek text reads "not yet" (oupo), whereas some early manuscripts read "not" (ouk), a variant reflecting how readers reconciled Jesus' statement here with His private ascent to the feast in verse 10.
notes.7:22: The phrase "Because of this" (dia touto) opens verse 22 in accordance with the Greek punctuation, though some interpreters attach it to the close of verse 21 ("and you all marvel because of this").
notes.7:38: The Greek word koilia literally means belly or womb and metaphorically denotes one's innermost being. While the Greek punctuation connects the rivers of living water to the believer, an early alternative punctuation joins "the one who believes in Me" to "let him drink" in verse 37, referring the rivers to Christ Himself.
notes.7:39: The Greek literally reads "for the Spirit was not yet," without the word "given"; it refers to the promised outpouring of the Spirit after Jesus' glorification rather than to the Spirit's eternal existence.
notes.7:46: The Greek text preserves the shorter reading "Never has a man spoken like this," whereas later manuscripts add "as this Man speaks."
notes.7:53: Text-critical double brackets ⟦ ⟧ are preserved verbatim from the Saints Greek Critical Text; the passage 7:53-8:11 is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts.
notes.8:1: Double brackets ⟦ ⟧ are preserved verbatim from the Saints Greek Critical Text throughout 8:1-11, marking a passage absent from the earliest Greek witnesses.
notes.8:6: The Saints Greek Critical Text includes the participial phrase me prospoioumenos ('taking no heed / acting as though He did not notice').
notes.8:7: Greek ton lithon carries the definite article ('the stone'), referring to the first stone in a stoning execution.
notes.8:9: The Saints Greek Critical Text includes kai hypo tes syneideseos elenchomenoi ('and being convicted by their conscience'), attested in the Byzantine textual tradition.
notes.8:11: Where verse 10 uses katekrinen ('condemned'), the Saints Greek Critical Text here reads the simple verb krino ('judge'), rendered distinctly.
notes.8:25: The Greek clause is notoriously difficult and may be construed either as an exasperated question (following the critical text's punctuation, "Why do I even speak to you at all?") or as a statement ("Just what I have been telling you from the beginning").
notes.8:38: The critical Greek text omits possessive pronouns in both clauses ("the Father" and "the father") and shifts from "seen with" to "heard from," leaving the true identity of their father unspoken until verse 44.
notes.8:54: The critical Greek text reads "our God" (quoting their own claim directly), whereas some later manuscripts change the pronoun to "your God."
notes.8:58: The Greek sharply contrasts the aorist "came into being" for Abraham with the timeless present "I am" for Jesus, echoing the divine self-designation of Exodus 3:14 and Isaiah 43:10 in the Greek Old Testament.
notes.8:59: The critical Greek text ends the chapter here, without the later manuscript expansion "going through the midst of them, and so passed by."
notes.9:4: The critical Greek text reads plural "We must" together with singular "who sent Me," associating the disciples with Jesus' mission; later manuscripts harmonize to "I must."
notes.9:24: "Give glory to God!" is an established biblical oath formula (cf. Joshua 7:19) adjuring the speaker to confess the truth before God.
notes.9:35: The earliest Greek manuscripts read "the Son of Man," whereas later witnesses read "the Son of God."
notes.9:36: Greek kyrie here may carry respectful address ("Sir") prior to Jesus' self-revelation, deepening into worshipful confession ("Lord") in verse 38.
notes.10:16: The Greek critical text reads the plural verb (they shall become one flock, one Shepherd), emphasizing the union of sheep from different folds, whereas later manuscripts read the singular (there shall be).
notes.10:18: The Greek critical text uses the aorist tense (has taken), emphasizing that no one has ever wrested Christ's life from Him, while later manuscripts read the present tense (takes).
notes.10:29: Following the earliest Greek witnesses with neuter forms, Jesus declares that what the Father has given Him is greater than all; many later manuscripts read masculine forms (My Father, who has given them to Me, is greater than all).
notes.10:38: The Greek critical text pairs the aorist and present subjunctives of the same verb (know and continue to know), underscoring both initial realization and abiding comprehension, whereas later manuscripts read know and believe.
notes.11:16: Didymus is the Greek equivalent of the Aramaic name Thomas, both meaning Twin.
notes.11:18: Fifteen stadia is approximately two miles (about 2.8 kilometers).
notes.11:33: The Greek verb embrimaomai (used again in 11:38) denotes intense inward agitation, encompassing both deep grief and righteous indignation in the face of death.
notes.11:35: John here shifts from klaio (weep aloud, lament, in 11:31, 33) to dakryo (shed tears), a verb occurring nowhere else in the New Testament.
notes.11:41: The earliest Greek manuscripts read simply So they removed the stone, whereas later manuscripts add from the place where the dead man was lying.
notes.12:6: The Greek verb ebastazen literally means "carried," but in the context of Judas being a thief it carries the sense of pilfering or taking from the money box.
notes.12:7: The critical Greek text reads "that she may keep it" (hina ... terese auto) rather than the later variant "she has kept this" (teterken), indicating that Mary was to reserve the ointment for Jesus' burial or that her anointing anticipated it.
notes.12:27: The clause "Father, save Me from this hour" can be read either as an earnest petition immediately yielded to the Father's purpose or as a deliberative question ("Shall I say, 'Father, save Me from this hour'?").
notes.12:41: The critical Greek text reads "because" (hoti) rather than the variant "when" (hote), underscoring that Isaiah spoke these words as a result of beholding Christ's glory (Isaiah 6:1–10).
notes.12:47: The critical Greek text reads "does not keep them" (me phylaxe) rather than the later textual variant "does not believe" (me pisteuse).
notes.13:1: Greek eis telos carries the twofold meaning "to the end" (temporally, through His impending death) and "to the uttermost" (to the fullest measure of love).
notes.13:10: Greek distinguishes two verbs here: louo ("bathe" the whole body) and nipto ("wash" a part, such as the feet). A few early manuscripts omit "except to wash his feet," though the phrase is retained in the Greek text translated here.
notes.13:19: Greek ego eimi ("I am") echoes the divine self-declaration of Exodus 3:14 and Isaiah 43:10, while also conveying the contextual sense "I am He."
notes.13:32: Some later manuscripts begin this verse with the clause "If God is glorified in Him," which is absent from the earlier witnesses followed in this text.
notes.14:1: The Greek form pisteuete can be read as either indicative ("you believe") or imperative ("believe") in both clauses, permitting a statement followed by a command or two parallel commands.
notes.14:2: Greek monai ("abodes" or "dwelling places") shares the same root as "abide" (meno) and "abode" (mone) in 14:23. Because the Greek includes hoti, the second clause can also be read as a question: "if it were not so, would I have told you that I am going to prepare a place for you?"
notes.14:14: Strong early manuscript witnesses include the pronoun "Me" (me), highlighting prayer directed to Jesus Himself, whereas some later manuscripts omit it.
notes.14:16: Greek parakletos ("Comforter") refers to one called alongside to console, strengthen, counsel, or plead as an advocate, and is variously rendered "Comforter," "Advocate," "Counselor," or "Helper."
notes.15:2: The Greek employs a play on words between airei ("removes") and kathairei ("prunes" or "cleanses"), linking directly to katharoi ("clean") in verse 3.
notes.15:8: The critical Greek text reads the subjunctive genesthe ("and become My disciples") rather than the future indicative ("you will be") found in some later manuscripts.
notes.15:10: The critical Greek text reads "the Father's commandments" (tou Patros) without the possessive pronoun "My."
notes.15:26: Greek parakletos ("Advocate") denotes one called alongside to plead, assist, counsel, or comfort, and is also translated "Helper," "Counselor," or "Comforter."
notes.16:16: The critical Greek text does not include "because I go to the Father" at the end of this verse; the disciples' quotation in verse 17 echoes Jesus' words in verse 10.
notes.16:23: In the critical Greek text, "in My name" follows "He will give it to you," highlighting that the Father's giving—as well as the disciples' asking (v. 24)—is granted in Christ's name.
notes.16:27: The critical Greek text reads "from God" (para tou theou), whereas some manuscripts harmonize to "from the Father."
notes.16:33: The critical Greek text reads the present tense echete ("you have tribulation"), depicting affliction as a present reality rather than only a future one.
notes.17:11: The Greek text reads "in Your name which You have given Me" (with the relative pronoun referring to the Father's name rather than to the disciples, as in some later manuscripts and similarly in 17:12).
notes.17:15: The Greek phrase "ek tou ponerou" can mean either "from evil" (neuter) or "from the evil one" (masculine), with Johannine usage favoring the personal reference to Satan.
notes.17:17: The verb "hagiazo" ("consecrate" or "sanctify") carries the sense of setting apart as holy for God's service, illuminating Jesus's words in 17:19 ("I consecrate Myself"); the critical text reads "in the truth" without "Your."
notes.17:24: The Greek uses a collective neuter singular ("that which You have given Me," as also in 17:2) followed by a masculine plural ("they also"), viewing believers together as the Father's unified gift to the Son.
notes.18:5: Jesus's reply "I am He" translates the Greek "ego eimi" (literally "I am"), echoing God's self-disclosure in the Scriptures and helping explain why the arresting party stepped back and fell to the ground in 18:6.
notes.18:13: Annas had served as high priest earlier (A.D. 6-15) and retained major influence and the courtesy title while his son-in-law Caiaphas held the official office that year.
notes.18:37: Jesus's reply "You say that I am a king" is a qualified affirmation acknowledging kingship while distancing Himself from Pilate's political sense of the title; some interpreters punctuate it as "You say so, for I am a king."
notes.18:40: The Greek term "lestes" ("robber" or "bandit") was frequently used in first-century Judea for violent rebels or insurrectionists.
notes.19:13: The Greek verb ekathisen can be taken intransitively ("took his seat upon the judgment seat") or transitively ("seated Him upon the judgment seat"), though the intransitive reading is standard. "In Hebrew" (Hebraisti) in John refers to the Aramaic tongue spoken in first-century Judea.
notes.19:14: By Jewish reckoning from sunrise, "about the sixth hour" is roughly noon; some interpreters harmonize this with Mark 15:25 ("the third hour") by understanding John to use Roman timekeeping from midnight (around 6:00 a.m.) or broad three-hour intervals of the day.
notes.19:25: The Greek wording allows either three women (taking "Mary the wife of Clopas" in apposition to "the sister of His mother") or four distinct women. Literally the Greek reads "Mary the [one] of Clopas," traditionally understood as his wife.
notes.19:28: The purpose clause "in order that the Scripture might be fulfilled" can be construed either with what precedes ("all things had now been accomplished") or with what follows (Jesus saying, "I thirst," echoing Psalm 69:21).
notes.19:39: A Roman pound (litra) was about twelve modern ounces (roughly 327 grams), so one hundred pounds equals approximately seventy-five modern pounds (about 34 kilograms), a royal quantity of burial spices.
notes.20:16: In the Greek text, Jesus addresses Mary with the Semitic form Mariam, and she replies in Aramaic/Hebrew with Rabboni, an elevated form of Rabbi meaning 'Teacher' or 'my Master.'
notes.20:17: The Greek present imperative 'Do not cling to Me' (literally 'Do not touch Me') implies ceasing an ongoing or attempted hold; the critical Greek text reads 'to the Father' rather than 'to My Father.'
notes.20:29: Following the critical Greek text, the vocative 'Thomas' is absent here, and the opening clause is rendered as a question ('Because you have seen Me, have you believed?').
notes.20:31: Greek manuscripts divide between the present subjunctive ('may continue to believe') and the aorist subjunctive ('may come to believe'); the present tense here encompasses both coming to faith and persevering in it.
notes.21:7: The Greek word gymnos ('naked') commonly denoted a fisherman or laborer who had laid aside his outer garment and was working lightly clad.
notes.21:15: The critical Greek text reads 'Simon, son of John' here and in verses 16-17 rather than 'son of Jonah,' and 'more than these' may refer to the other disciples, to their devotion, or to Peter's fishing livelihood.
notes.21:17: Across verses 15-17, the Greek alternates between agapao and phileo for 'love,' bosko ('feed') and poimaino ('shepherd'), and terms for 'lambs' and 'sheep' (a diminutive form in verse 17); while some see a deliberate nuance, John frequently uses such pairs as stylistic synonyms.
notes.21:25: The critical Greek text ends here without the closing liturgical 'Amen' added in later manuscripts.
